title: Icom manual notch filter frequency
body:
I'm in the process of fixing implementation of many Icom CI-V commands that currently either do not work at all or work incorrectly when compared to the Hamlib API spec.

However, there's one particular command that is difficult to implement with Icom radios and that is the manual notch frequency (`RIG_LEVEL_NOTCHF`). Based on Icom radio manuals I've read (and I've checked most of the modern ones >= IC-7000), the scale for adjusting manual notch frequency is simply 0 to 255 without any indication of the actual frequency.

After all, the Hamlib API specifies `RIG_LEVEL_NOTCHF` as:
```
    RIG_LEVEL_NOTCHF =      (1 << 15),      /*!< \c NOTCHF -- Notch Freq., arg int (Hz) */
```
indicating that the argument should be the frequency in Hz.

I'm wondering if anyone knows better whether the notch frequency value for Icom rigs actually corresponds to a specific frequency or if it is relative to, for example, the filter width currently selected?

title: Filter width setting doesn't work with data mode on Icom
body:
`icom_set_mode_with_data` calls `icom_set_mode`, passing the filter width through, and then does a data mode (`1A 06`, except on IC-7200) call to set data mode to 0 or 1 depending on whether the mode was a `PKT` one.

The problem is that (at least on the 7300 and 7610, and probably on most newer rigs), the filter width passed to the "set mode" command only affects the *non-data* filter width, and to change the data filter width, one must pass a filter width to the `1A 06` command. Since hamlib omits this parameter, the width is never changed for packet modes.

It seems easy enough to drag a call to `rig2icom_mode`/`r2i_mode` into `icom_set_mode_with_data` to get the proper width and then pass it along to the datamode command, but perhaps a refactor is in order — should there be one function which outputs `icmode`/`icmode_ext`/`datamode`/`datamode_ext` and the whole sequence keyed off of those?

Also, to research: are there rigs that support 1A 06, but where it doesn't have a second byte for filter width?

title: Generating a Hamlib.pdf
body:
Hi (my first issue). I'm on Windows trying to build a `HamLib.pdf` using Cygwin's tool
*texi2any* and *MikTeX* with this command in `doc`.
```
/bin/texi2any --pdf hamlib.texi
```
(yes, I have created a `doc/version.texi` first). But is errors with:

hamlib.texi:52: @menu seen before first @node
hamlib.texi:52: perhaps your @top node should be wrapped in @ifnottex rather than @ifinfo?

But with this simple patch, the `HamLib.pdf` was created just fine:
```diff
--- a/doc/hamlib.texi 2019-10-10 18:09:37
+++ b/doc/hamlib.texi 2019-10-11 08:14:06
@@ -47,7 +47,6 @@

 This manual is for Ham Radio Control Libraries (Hamlib) (version @value{VERSION},
 @value{UPDATED}).
-@end ifnottex

 @menu
 * Copying and Redistribution::
@@ -59,6 +58,7 @@
 * List of Figures::
 * Concept Index::
 @end menu
+@end ifnottex
```
Does this makes sense?

title: Icom PCR-100 default output volume too low and windows help
body:
Hello,  I am very involved in many educational projects with the
International Space Station.

In these projects, I need to use "rigctld" to control my receiver and
correct Doppler effects.

I use the ICOM PCR-100 model with GPredict software. However, with this
receiver, when you take control of it with HAMLib, the volume of the
output sound is too low.

To control the receiver, I use this command on linux :

rigctld -v -m 402 -r /dev/ttyUSB0 -s 38400 -t 4532 -C stop_bits=1

And a kind of this one on Windows :

"C:Program Files\HAMLib\rigctld.exe" -v -m 402 -r /dev/ttyUSB0 -s 38400
-t 4532 -C stop_bits=1

To increase the output volume on Linux, the only way I've found is to
open a second terminal window and to use this command to set up the volume to the maximum :

echo 'L AF 1' | nc localhost 4532

But I didn't find any way to do the same on Windows.

So here are my questions : How can we take control of the receiver with
the output volume set to the maximum without having to open a second terminal window and using another command line ? If there is no way to do that, how can I use the same command on Windows to set the volume at its maximum ?

Thanks for the answer.

Best regards, David.

title: Automated testing of device backends
body:
(Tried to post this to the mailing list, but it looks like it didn't get through, so I'm reposting here)

Please correct if I'm wrong, but it seems there are currently no tests for individual radio/rotator backends in Hamlib.

I'm seeing this as a big issue, since it is very easy to cause regressions in individual radio commands when refactoring and/or adding new functionality to an existing backend. I've experienced this multiple times during the last year when developing a web-based remote control UI that uses Hamlib to control radios. The basic commands (frequency, mode, VFO) work very well, but in case of controlling a remote station also the Hamlib function and level controls become very important.

I'd really like to take Hamlib "to the next level" in 2019 regarding reliability and completeness of backend command sets by introducing a testing framework for both radio backends and later also for rotator backends.

This framework would mock the normal serial/parallel/USB I/O routines (which is luckily possible because of the excellent I/O abstractions in Hamlib) and do the following:

1. Run a globally defined set of test cases, which would include every single Hamlib command with a predefined set of parameters
2. For each command, the mock routines would
2.1. record the output of all write()-type commands for a particular command
2.2. compare it to a backend-specific byte array for a specific test case
2.3. offer a backend-specific byte array for a specific test case as a response for all read()-type commands
2.4. check the expected return value of the Hamlib command executed

Every test case would naturally need a unique identifier so that the global test framework could search for valid test cases for each backend. Backend would need to register a data structure containing the test case expectations for the command output and return value and the device response to be offered to the backend.

In order to develop and to extend the set of test cases, a missing test case would not indicate a failure, but we could generate a HTML matrix similar to the rig command support matrix containing the test cases executed and present for each backend.

What I'd like to accomplish with this setup is:

A) When making changes to Hamlib code, we could verify that each and every Hamlib command still outputs the same device-specific command for a specific backend and that the backend interprets device responses, including errors, correctly. There have been cases where simple changes to, for example, fix compiler warnings have resulted in broken code (I saw one with IC-7300 backend last year).

B) When adding new functionality it would become more apparent when to branch code for a new model: e.g. Elecraft KX3/K3/K3s have many similar commands, but are not 100% compatible -- yet they share the backend code. There should always be a good reason to change the expected output of a test, so nothing would go unnoticed.

Adding test data for all backends is a huge task and will need a lot of effort from the whole Hamlib developer community, but I think automated testing is the _only_ way forward if we wish to keep Hamlib usable and maintainable when we are making breaking changes (like now for 4.0 release). In addition, the list of supported hardware keeps on growing and radios are becoming more complex with wider sets of features, which certainly does not make Hamlib development easier :)

Please share your thoughts about this kind of effort. If you feel this change would be welcome, I can continue by posting more detailed design in GitHub.

73,
Mikael OH3BHX

title: Machine-readable data format / capabilities
body:
The current data format of rigctld/rotctld responses is quite hard to parse -- especially the capabilities list is a bit of a nightmare. I've been thinking of introducing an alternate data format, e.g. JSON, for this purpose.

There are also some other issues with rig capabilities listings: currently they do not contain all of the information specified in the rig backends. At least TX/RX ranges and ext level definitions (numeric ranges / combo choices) are missing.

Now that the project is heading towards a new major release with possibility of breaking API/ABI, it could be a good time to introduce this kind of change. Obviously we would need a flag/option to specify which data format to use, so that the old one could be preserved for backwards-compatibility.

I'd just like to hear maintaners' opinions/ideas on this to decide whether it makes sense to proceed with implementation. Depending on the data format, we would need to add new dependencies, e.g. jansson for JSON.

title: Handling for waterfall/bandscope data on Icom SDR rigs
body:
Icom SDR rigs (7300, 7610, 9700, etc.) support sending waterfall data over USB for display on a PC. When the scope data output (command 27 subcommand 20) is enabled, the rig sends a constant stream of unsolicited scope data reports (command 27 subcommand 00), with raw binary payloads, between command responses. Their RS-BA1 remote control software and a few other third-party Windows programs support decoding and displaying it.

I want to make something similar but cross-platform, and of course I don't want my program to take sole ownership of the serial port; I want to have rigctld running and do other hamlib things at the same time. Practically speaking, this means that hamlib needs to be the one handling the scope data.

I don't care if hamlib *interprets* it, but what I would hope for would be

* For hamlib not to desync or show any behavior difference to uninterested clients, when connected to a rig with scope data output enabled.
* For a TCP client to have a way to subscribe to the scope data, receiving it as it comes in, with sensible framing (It could also be used for other kinds of transcieve data, e.g. Icoms will tell you about frequency changes and PTT toggles if you ask... but I don't care if it doesn't). I wouldn't mind if starting one of these subscriptions made the socket totally unable to issue other commands (to avoid framing problems).

I think this should be more or less possible with the existing event loop code in hamlib, and I'm willing to make an attempt at it myself, but I wanted to run the approach by someone first, and get some input, to increase the chances of actually getting a patch accepted.

title: Hamlib does not handle Yaesu FT-900 CAT commands properly.
body:
I have found that Hamlib (and indeed other software) does not handle FT-900 CAT commands properly.

The FT-900 will always return the command you send it as the first 5 bytes of the output.

For example, the following command (note reversed order, in hex):  `00 00 00 03 10`
will yield the following in my case:

`00 00 00 03 10 06 16 20 76 00 00 01 04 02 04 0B BF D0 00 00 00 04 00`

Note that the first five bytes are equivalent to the command I sent, and is followed with 18 additional bytes containing the VFO data, totaling 23 bytes.

For your development purposes, this is the radio configuration I had at the time:

VFO-A = 14.50102 MHz USB
VFO-B =  7.70000 MHz LSB

This matches the data provided on page 46 of the FT-900 manual (reference http://biara.org/wp-content/uploads/2017/08/2D-FT-900.pdf)

I don't believe that this is being handled in /yaesu/FT900.c -- ft900_get_update_data doesn't handle it at all.

In particular, reference [ft900.c line 508](https://github.com/Hamlib/Hamlib/blob/7c7ecef678c62eaed10bacab548f99f64ce65811/yaesu/ft900.c#L508): It explicitly sets the count as FT900_VFO_DATA_LENGTH, defined [here](https://github.com/Hamlib/Hamlib/blob/7c7ecef678c62eaed10bacab548f99f64ce65811/yaesu/ft900.h#L65).  On [line 528](https://github.com/Hamlib/Hamlib/blob/7c7ecef678c62eaed10bacab548f99f64ce65811/yaesu/ft900.c#L528), `ft900_get_update_data` is called, which is defined on [line 1639](https://github.com/Hamlib/Hamlib/blob/7c7ecef678c62eaed10bacab548f99f64ce65811/yaesu/ft900.c#L1639).  The bug exists on [line 1662](https://github.com/Hamlib/Hamlib/blob/7c7ecef678c62eaed10bacab548f99f64ce65811/yaesu/ft900.c#L1662) and beyond:  `read_block` only reads the number of octets defined under the parameter `rl`, which we saw before was defined as 18.  In this instance, the resultant decoded frequency will _always_ be incorrect, since the data read starts with `00 00 00 03 10` -- as the code stands, the routine will decode bytes 1-3, `00 00 03` = 30 Hz.  Since this is outside of the RX and TX under `rx_range_listN` and `tx_range_listN`, this will _ALWAYS_ generate an error.

I don't see anywhere in the manual where this is referenced, but this is the behavior of my own FT-900 as it stands.  Perhaps for safety, only read the 18 bytes and check whether the first 5 match the command that was just sent, and if so, read an extra 5 bytes?

Please let me know if you need any testing with the FT-900.  I am happy to help.

title: Hamlib error: IO error while opening connection to rig (FT-991A)
body:
Since two days I get errors after starting WSJT-X (version 2.1.0) running on my Win10 PC which is connected to my FT-991A. 
I am using this configuration already since 2 months without any problems. The mentioned problem started last sunday after I made a QSO in the mode C4FM. I tried to start WSJT-X again but got a error message HAMLib could not read the mode. In the first place I was not aware the this probably had to do with the C4FM-mode I selected on my FT-991a. So after some try  and error I reset my config in WSJT-X and reconfigured it. Still the same error message refering to HAMLib. So I decided to remove HamLib and reinstalled it with version 3.3.

All com-ports and as well as the audio interface work properly. And are not reinstalled. Als Windows does not show any disconnection of the comports. No hardware has been changed. USB cable is OK and provided with several RF beads MIX31. 

I googled and found more same problems that rever to this HamLib IO error. 
Please help!
73's PA3VOS

body:
I'm using rigctl 3.3 and I realize the TH-D72a driver is ALPHA but I was doing some testing for an upcoming project things didn't get off to a good start.

I start things off with:
rigctld -m 233 -r /dev/ttyUSB0 -s9600 -vvvvv

Then I launch gpredict, where I have the radio configured in preferences as Duplex TRX, PTT Status=none, and VFO up/down is MAIN up/SUB down.

When I bring up the GPredict Radio Control panel and click Engage, it connects to rigctld but after several attempts and some errors, it fails and disconnects from rigctld.

title: Update wiki/Supported Rotators, add macro name
body:
When using Hamlib via the Python bindings (e.g. in [satnogsclient:satnogsclient/observer/worker.py#L134)](https://gitlab.com/librespacefoundation/satnogs/satnogs-client/-/blob/master/satnogsclient/observer/worker.py#L134)) generated by swig, the rotator model must be provided using the rotator model macros. To allow users to get the model name without looking into the source code of Hamlib (macro defines at [rotlist.h](https://github.com/Hamlib/Hamlib/blob/4c47ff4f9315788566a26a5996f34d45406ccd1a/include/hamlib/rotlist.h)), I added the macro names to a list of supported rotators, based on the list from the wiki. Additionally I added missing models, fixed a typo in the heading and introduced the use of markdown-syntax tables.

Please consider to update the wiki page [Supported Rotators](https://github.com/Hamlib/Hamlib/wiki/Supported-Rotators) with the following table (this should be able via copy-paste. title: Flex 6xxx interface sets mode to first mode in list (narrowest)
body:
Hi All,

Log4OM V2 ver 2.2.4 now supports IP connection to the Flex 6xxx series radios using Hamlib. 

The issue I am finding is when clicking on a DX spot in the cluster it is QSYing, setting mode, then setting RX filter to narrowest for that mode (50 Hz on CW, 1.8 kHz on SSB). 

OmniRig does not exhibit this behavior.

Is there a way to have Hamlib QSY and set mode but NOT set filter?

Thanks from Hamlib newbie.

Dave wo2x

title: rotctl: broken/stuttering control of G-5500 with GS-232B
body:
Hi Folks,
I have a G-5500 rotator and GS-232B controller. I am driving the controller through a USB->RS232 converter (Prolific pl2303 converter) from a raspberry pi.

When I try driving the rotator with rotctl, the rotator moves, but stutters (i.e. what should be a single drive to the new az/el is broken up). When I drive the rotator directly via the GS-232B (using ```screen /dev/ttyUSB0``` to directly use the serial port), there is no such problem.

the output of rotctl is below:
```

Having looked through the code a bit, the core of the command seems to be the gs232b_transaction() function, which writes a command then waits for a reply. So question is: have I missed something in the use of rotctl here? Or maybe something has changed in the behaviour of the GS-232B compared to the past?

Randall

Perhaps depending on whether or not they actually do anything.  AI0 has been run so transceive is off so this appears to be errant behavior.
Will have to change so that IF is a valid response for those two commands to avoid the repeat that occurs.

title: Rotctl get_pos and set_pos errors with Meade driver
body:
Hi,

I am running rotctl and rotctld (release 3.3) on Win 10 64-bit with a Meade Starnavigator az/el mount with a 497EP Audiostar controller.  Per multiple sources, this hand controller is fully backward compatible with classic Meade Autostar protocol, and this is more or less confirmed by successful operation in other applications.

The connection looks fine, and I can confirm the mount receives command, per Issue 2 below.
```
c:\Program Files (x86)\hamlib-w32-3.3\bin>rotctl -m 1801 -r COM3 -vvvv
rotctl, Hamlib 3.3
Report bugs to <hamlib-developer@lists.sourceforge.net>

rot_init called
meade: _init called
rot_register (1801)
meade_init called
rot_open called
serial_open called
serial_setup called
meade_open called
serial_flush called
write_block called
Opened rot model 1801, 'LX200'
rig_strstatus called
Backend version: 0.1, Status: Alpha
```


**Issue 1**:  get_pos returns "Invalid parameter"
```
Rotator command: p
rot_get_position called
meade_get_position called
serial_flush called
write_block called
read_string called
get_pos: error = Invalid parameter
```

This appears to be the same issue as previously reported here: 
https://sourceforge.net/p/hamlib/mailman/message/36799731/  

**Issue 2**:  set_pos fails if _elevation_ argument greater than 1.50 deg (regardless of az which works fine for elevation values <=1.5).  Here's a successful slew to 1.5 deg and failure at 1.51:
```
Rotator command: P 10 1.50
Azimuth: Elevation: rot_set_position called
meade_set_position called: 10.00 1.50
serial_flush called
write_block called
read_string called
serial_flush called
write_block called
read_string called

Rotator command: P 10 1.51
Azimuth: Elevation: rot_set_position called
meade_set_position called: 10.00 1.51
serial_flush called
write_block called
read_string called
serial_flush called
write_block called
read_string called
set_pos: error = Invalid parameter
```

This seems suspiciously close to 1.57 rad, which is 90 deg elevation, which one might expect to get rejected.  I wonder if there might be a missing deg->rad conversion?

Logs available if needed, but the above snippets capture the parts of interest.

Thanks

title: IC-910H acts differently now (snapshot build 20200504 vs 20200405)
body:
To give you insight, I'm using Gpredict + rigctld to control my radio + rotctld to control my rotator. 

Previously, I was using **20200405 snapshot build** which worked incredibly well on IC-910 to Gpredict to GQRX. In Gpredict radio controller, I always select an interface I created named "GQRX" localhost, port 7356 as my receive, and another interface "IC910" localhost, port 4532 as my transmit (this requires only the MAIN band to be active). My radio is configured to only show MAIN BAND, the SUB BAND is hidden/disabled for this. After pressing "ENGAGE" from Gpredict, then I turn the physical vfo knob on the radio, I could see whatever frequency I have on the radio will be displayed in Gpredict radio control. And the frequency stays to where ever I left it. Vice versa, if I will adjust the uplink/downlink from gpredict, radio frequency follows thru **I could control the freq in two ways, gpredict to radio or radio to gpredict.**

Sometimes I don't use the "GQRX". and have the "IC910" be my rx and tx, so my radio needs to be in satellite mode for this prior to running rigctld. After pressing ENGAGE, I could see whatever frequency I have on the MAIN and SUB band from the radio will be displayed in Gpredict radio control both for Downlink and Uplink. Turn the knob from radio, GPredict will update. Stop turning the knob, frequency stays where ever I left it. **I could control the freq in two ways, gpredict to radio or radio to gpredict.**


The above **previously** worked great! Until...

Using the latest **20200505 snapshot build**, after engaging - then I turn the physical vfo knob on the radio, I could see the frequency reflected back to Gpredict "momentarily" then go back again to original frequency (the update speed is controlled by XXX msec "cycle" from Gpredict). 
Right now, I couldn't use the knob on my radio to control/update Gpredict uplink/downlink anymore, it's only one-way (Gpredict to radio,YES) but (radio to gpredict "no longer usable")

I tried to report this as clear as possible, but if you have any questions or need anymore clarification, I am willing to provide more feedback.

title: FT-DX101D alternating VFOS when split is used
body:
Selecting option FT-dx101D in JTDX radio tab and using SPLIT mode ('Rig' option in JTDX) causes alternating VFO-A to VFO-B switching during TX.

Setup:
Yaesu FTdx101D linked to the Yaesu SCU-17 interface which is connected to a laptop
RTS is not used (RTS is not supported via serial interface of radio itself) so the CAT command to PTT is used instead
Baud Rate 38400
FT-dx101D radio selected in JTDX

Findings:

When SPLIT mode is not selected all seems fine (positive). When SPLIT mode is enabled, the radio alternates between VFO-A and VFO-B. A second receiving radio observed the incorrect TX frequency used when (the incorrect) VFO-A was selected for TX. In case of when radio FT-dx3000 model is selected in JTDX, this alternating VFO-a to VFO-B is not present. (But causes other issues, read on).

title: IC-910 frequency while transmitting
rig_get_channel inconsistent
body:
rig_get_channel is inconsistently implemented.
Some backends update the rig and some don't.
So we will add a read_only flag to the call so the client can ask for a channel and leave the rig as it was. 
Each backend will have to allow for read only and restoring the rig values if needed.
For the moment just the flag has been added and a number of #warn comments inserted about backends that need more changes.
We will also add a flag to rigctl/rigctld on the "h" command to allow read only.  So "h 2 0" will read channel 2 and update the rig and "h 2 1" will read the channel and leave the rig as it was.

title: Lack of sufficent Pi documentation
body:
- GPIO support is left out of man pages
- use examples of how to use hamlib with GPIO pins for PTT do not exist in documentation
- no raspberry pi specific build instructions in the wiki's documentation (nor in the install documentation for compiling for use on a pi)

Reason for update: many hams are turning to Pi's for cheap shack computers. Also many hams do not have the ability to control their rig through a cable (most HT's, older rigs and DIY kits) or otherwise do not want the added overhead (might be backpacking and every extra cable adds weight and a fail point). Most Digital Station setups (see the NW Digital Radio's DRAW/UDRC boards and WB7FHC's Nexus Board for examples) require the use of a GPIO pin to control the PTT on a radio (or radios). I would love to use wspr modes with my pi, but due to the lack of documentation I cannot figure out how to use hamlib to key the rig through a GPIO pin. Also with no steps in recompiling the library for use on the pi I have no way of testing to see if it works.

I'd be happy to help with testing and examples (application specific as well) if you need it.

73
Art - KC7SDA

body:
Hi Mike

Trying to set up IF width and IF shift sliders

Using the scope decode:

\get_level Main IF     - this reads IF shift *CAT manual:  IS...

rig IF shift set to +980Hz

return on scope is: IS00+0980;    - good!

return from command line rigctl is:  0

rig IF shift set to -1160Hz

return on scope is:    IS00-1160;

return from command line rigctl is:   0

You are sending the correct command - but not interpreting the result

I then send:   \set_level Main IF -346   -    No effect on the rig

Scope decode of rigctl send is:  IS0-0346;

rigctl should have responded:   IS00-0346;  
(ie: I  S  P1   P2  P3  P4(4 chars) 
P1 = 0 = Main    P2 = 0  (fixed)   P3 - or +    P4 4 data chars 0-1200Hz

//////////////////////////////

VOX delay   - there seems to be an error in the Yaesu CAT manual here

From the manual, Vox delay 00:  30msec      01: 50msec     02 100ms   ie non linear ... I use a lookup table
So I set 100ms  (data = 02 )
I send \get_level Main VOXDELAY       rigctl returns: 0

Scope decode:  VD; (correct)     response VD02;  
My piWebCAT config for the response is 5 bytes:    VDtu;   (mapped as tens and units)

BUT .. the manual says V   D    P1   P1   P1   P1    ;   =   7 bytes  !!!!

....is this the problem???

In my initial comments on checking out these commands with rigctl,
I was only commenting on failed responses  .... not incorrect responses!!

The persistent zero responses were VOXDELAY, ANTIVOX and IF

The rest are I think ok  -.... I haven' tset them all up yet.

///////////////////

I thought IF width was absent - but of course it is returned by \get_mode   - which is already working here.

I will use   \get_mode    AND  \set_mode   separately for the IF width slider
The result will have two separate parsing results - but they will be Hamlib-specific and
apply to all rigs  - so can be hard coded for Hamlib operation.

/////////////////////

Thanks be to the Siglent SDS2202X-E scope
I dont think i could have  developed piWebCAT without it
  .... particularly for FT920  FT1000MkV where the documentation in incomplete.
(I have a FT920 here)



Kind regards

Ian

title: Improving release quality / Review process for commits?
body:
As an active user of Hamlib (and also having developed some features in it), I'm wondering if we could implement some process and/or automation to improve the release quality -- especially to cut the number of regressions between releases. I know this is a particularly difficult software project from the aspect of testing, because it deals with real hardware, which is in most cases not available for the maintainers.

However, I think that we could still do _something_ for this matter.

My thoughts:

1. Would the maintainers be willing to start using a simple PR review process, where another maintainer would review and approve the PR? That said, I can volunteer here to be one of the reviewers if the maintainers accept me :) The exact details of approval process need to be agreed, of course. Having "no merges without approval by someone else" may be too strict for this project, but for most non-urgent work, this could be a really good solution.

2. Implement a way to test current functionality with real hardware, e.g. something along the lines of #263 

3. Implement "mock ports" for serial/parallel/ethernet ports to capture input/output from the backends to test for regressions. This could be an extension to #263 where the code is run against a "mock rig". I know this would a lot of work, but it could save a lot of time fixing errors later on.

Thoughts?

We could start number 1 (PR review process) fairly quickly if we can agree on details!

title: CW Morse stop command

labels.name: Needs test
labels.description: Patches have been submitted but need testing to close issue

body:
HI!

Rigctld sends morse with command "b" if rig supports it. Different rigs
have different sizes to buffer the text to be sent.
When rig is sending CW sometimes there is need to stop transmit immediately.

With keyboard operation (contests etc.) normal way is to hit ESC to
cause CW to stop. Now if rigctld keyer is in use implementing the "CW
stop" is bit hard for client software as every rig uses it's own way.

Sending a rigctld message that have "b\0xFF" will stop CW at least with
ic7300 (maybe with all modern icoms?). Sending empty message (buffer
full of spaces) should stop sending with Kenwood TS480 (by manual, not
tested)

Has there been any discussions to implement "stop morse" command to
rigctld so that clients could use only that and rigctld would convert it
to suitable command using current rig's library data ?


--
Saku
OH1KH

title: End of CW indication
body:
Lately I have been thinking a way to change CW speed on the fly. It seems to be impossible at least with IC7300 and hamlib as there is no proper "end of buffer" indication.

With Winkeyer(USB) it is easy to create a CW macro   "tu +++5nn--- 123" A contest message where report is sent faster than other text. + increases and - decreases speed (this case programmed 5WPM/mark).

When IC7300 is sending CW via hamlib speed can be changed up and down but timing does not work. With a short  macro string above IC7300 will send all text, then raise and lower speed when text is already sent.

We could split string to "tu ", "+++5nn" and "---123" and it would work if we just could get indication that last letter of string is sent.
I even tried to send the string letter by letter but even that did not succeed. It should, but when letter is still going out it reports RPRT0 and that is the only feedback and if it is used to release next letter, or speed change, the timing is wrong.

I even  considered to make WPM calculated delay to top level program for feeding letters but not yet tried it. How ever it would be more or less blind way to find buffer end.

All this might be impossible because of rig's CAT way controlling CW but I have not studied it at serial connection binary level, so this should be checked, too.

title: Gpredict FT-817/TH-D74 behavior on manual frequency change

labels.name: Needs test
labels.description: Patches have been submitted but need testing to close issue

labels.name: Critical
labels.description: A problem for common operations with WSJT-X, GPredict, RigPi, etc.

body:
Using Gpredict with the latest version of hamlib (4.0 rc2), when satellite tracking is engaged, a manual change of the frequency using the rig knob is overridden. E.g., if the downlink frequency is 145.740 before Doppler, this is not changed when turning the knob of the rig. Gpredict forces the frequency back to 145.740 plus/minus Doppler.

This happens in Windows and Linux, both with FT-817 and TH-D74 connected via Bluetooth. It works with TH-D74 if I change the cycle to 5000 ms or keeping 1000 ms and moving the knob very fast. With FT-817 it doesn’t work as the cycle doesn’t seem to influence the frequency update interval.

title: IC7000 --vfo mode Problem switching to VFOB
body:
IC7000   
VFO switching was fine with rigctld when not using --vfo mode

In --vfo mode

If I switch to VFOB with piWebCAT I then get fast oscillatory switching
between VFOs
- assumed reason: There are ongoing repetitive reads of various parameters 
  which are use  VFOA as dummy parameter in the command.

and every read flips to VFOA and back to VFOB

Investigating:

With VFOA selected
    U VFOA NR 1    works fine
    U VFOB NR 1 flips the rig to VFOB and then immediately back to VFOA

With VFOB selected
  U VFOB NR 1 works fine
  U VFOA NR 1 flips the rig to VFOA and then immediately back to VFOB

More importantly, my piWebCAT software is doing repetitve synchonising reads
for selected on-screen controls. eg: u VFOA NR

On testing this at the command line with VFOB selected:
  u VFOA NR flips the VFO selection to VFOA and then immediately back to VFOB (reads NR correctly)
I think it is the stream of repetitive such reads that is causing the oscillating behaviour.

I am in --vfo mode so I have to use VFOA as a dummy parameter 

I think its ok if I use  u VFOB NR  with VFOB selected.  - but \get_vfo is not supported

Ian
G3VPX

title: FTDX101 control issues
body:
I've done some thorough testing on an FTDX101 (only accessible to me remotely via Hamlib) and found the following issues with the latest master on Oct 19th 2020.

Rig model in Hamlib is:
```
  1040  Yaesu                  FT-DX101D               20201016.5      Stable      RIG_MODEL_FTDX101D
```

- [x] FM mode is missing (PKTFM is there)
- [x] FM / AM filters cannot be used (only 2 filters?) -- changing filter width has no effect
- [x] Check if FTDX101 supports freely adjustable filter width (filter width 0 in Hamlib)
- [x] MIC GAIN range is incorrect (only 0-40 when it should be 0-100%)
- [x] COMP cannot be turned off (but no error)
- [x] MONITOR cannot be turned on (but no error)
- [x] LOCK cannot be turned off
- [x] Meters added: S-meter, comp meter, RF power meter, current, voltage
- [x] Fixed '+\get_ctcss_tone' fails with response: Communication timed out (error code -5)
- [x] Fixed incorrect scale for RF POWER
- [x] SPLIT verified to work correctly
- [x] RIT/XIT verified to work correctly, removed automatic enabling of RIT/XIT when adjusting offset frequency

I'll be fixing (hopefully most of) these in the coming days and will be updating this issue, but I thought I'd leave this open if I don't get all of them fixed.

title: Comm failure, TS-870S
body:
I recently lost the ability to control my TS-870 after an ubuntu update (which updated hamlib to 3.1). I observed that I could talk to the rig with minicom and it would respond to CAT commands. But, fldigi and flrig would not communicate with the radio. I invoked rigcat from the command line and kept getting a Protocol Error message:

ehidle@**redacted**:~/software/hamlib-3.3$ rigctl -r /dev/ttyUSB2 -m 210 -D 19200
rig_open: error = Protocol error 

The "CTRL" indicator in the radio's display does illuminate when trying to communicate with hamlib. 

One other thing I noticed was that sometimes when I started minicom, I would see a string of commands load up the terminal as soon as it was opened, as if hamlib had tried to send them to the serial port but for some reason the serial port was not accepting them. That doesn't happen every time but I noticed it once or twice while trying to debug this.

Hamlib is working fine for all of my other radios (TS-590S, TS-590SG, TS-790A, TS-950SDX). I compiled 3.3 from source and the problem persists.

@mdblack98 I'm wondering what hardware this particular commit is based on:

https://github.com/Hamlib/Hamlib/commit/5a6a58f4783a5e59576a56cd36081d8afdb4137f

I've got a Prosistel D controller box for a PST61D rotator available for testing and the official documentation from Prosistel, which both indicate that the angles are degrees (not 1/10ths of degrees). Additionally, it is an error to query for elevation on an azimuth-only rotator controller.

I can fix both of these issues and make separate models for az / el / az+el rotators, which use the correct commands.

title: Extending rotator control API
body:
I've developed a custom network-based rotator backend for use at our local club house. The controller is Arduino Due based and the code is open-source, available in GitHub: https://github.com/mikaelnousiainen/oh3aarot-controller

The controller offers precise speed control, which is currently not easily possible to implement with the Hamlib rotator API, as one can specify rotation speed only with the move command and not with set az/el commands at all. There's also no possibility to use the "previous/default" speed with the move command.

Before I make any changes, would the following improvements be accepted in the rotator API:

1. Add a `ROT_SPEED_NOCHANGE` (possibly with a value of `0`) for the `move` command to indicate that the previous or a default speed should be used. The speed range should anyway be 1-100 (though not all rotator backends obey this and I could fix it too), as documented in the man pages.

2. Add rotator levels with a standard level for speed, so that it can be controlled without rotation.

3. Add read-only indicators (possibly via funcs?) to provide better visibility in sensors like CW/CCW limit reached, or CW/CCW threshold passed (for over 360 degree rotation support).

The existing backends would most likely need minimal changes and the level/func commands could simply follow the implementaitons of their rigctl equivalents.

title: Yaesu break-in delay scale
body:
@mdblack98 I'm trying to fix more bugs in Yaesu CAT commands (will be able to test on FTDX 5000 and FT-991 now) and ran into some issues, as I couldn't understand how the conversion for break-in delay from tenths-of-dots per second to milliseconds goes.

I'm seeing two conversions here, which don't match at all:

When setting the delay, conversion is a simple multiplication by 100: https://github.com/Hamlib/Hamlib/blob/master/rigs/yaesu/newcat.c#L3178

But when getting the delay, conversion is 5000 / value: https://github.com/Hamlib/Hamlib/blob/master/rigs/yaesu/newcat.c#L3931

Neither of those make sense to me... what does the "tenths-of-dots" per second mean? At what speed?

title: rigctld loses connection
body:
When rigctl is connected to rigctld and rigctld loses it's connection rigctld never recovers.
rigctld has to be restarted.
This is due to not recognizing retcode==2 as needing to reopen the rig.

title: Error message return
body:
Add function to retrieve last message generated in rig_debug statements.
So when a hamlib rig function returns an error we can also provide context and reason.

Comments in code said 1 stop bit was "assumed" so we're changing the assumption to 2 stop bits.

title: FTDX3000 with Signalink hamlib error

labels.name: Critical
labels.description: A problem for common operations with WSJT-X, GPredict, RigPi, etc.

body:
Error setting frequency occurring with FTDX3000, SignaLink, and VOX keying.

newcat.c is using ptt cache to determine ptt status and needs to query active ptt instead.

FTDX3000 cannot set either VFO when in split mode and PTT is on.

title: WSJTX JS8Call set_split on KX3 calling for VFO_SUB

labels.name: Critical
labels.description: A problem for common operations with WSJT-X, GPredict, RigPi, etc.

body:
Description of problem:
Hamlib fails to set a split VFO. Can be seen with rigctl, WSJSTX, and JS8Call.
This is a regression from hamlib-4.0-0.9.fc33.20200615git779cd69287.x86_64.

hamlib-4.0-0.13.20201126gitd8be93350f.fc33.x86_64
hamlib-4.0-2.fc33.x86_64

Configure WSJSTX and configure to use Elecraft KX3 and click on tune button. Or
run rigctl using Kx3 for the rig.

1. Start JS8Call in a terminal window
2. Configure to use Elecraft KX3 for rig control.
3. press the "Tune" button

title: FTdx101D RIT, XIT, PTT v o chnaging behvious

labels.name: Needs test
labels.description: Patches have been submitted but need testing to close issue

body:
piWebCAT has the means for the user to configure selected controls
to be repetitively updated from the corresponding rig status.
( Selected ... because to do them all would use too much CAT bandwidth)

When I switched the rig to Sub Rcvr, I noticed the receiver selection oscillating 
between Main and Sub receivers.
I found that the guilty items were PTT (obligatory) adn RIT and XIT (user optional)

Part of the problem was that these are NOT receiver specific commands 
and so I was using Main as a dummy parameter.   eg: j Main

The careful investigion report below explains the oscillatory behaviour:
 -- see j Main with rcvr = Sub 

All other  none-reciever-specific controls have no problem with using
Main as a dummy parameter.    eg: l Main NR

An obvious option from the rigctl command line based report is to use Sub as the
dummy prameter rather than Main..... as no rcvr chnage was noted.
**However, the behaviour was different with rigctld in piWebCAT and I still 
had the ocillatory behavior.**

piWebCAT web browser client sends a vx parameter to the server from a button, 
a button group or a slider control. 
This is 'X' if none-rcvr-specific or 'A' or 'B' if rcvr specific.
For 'A' and 'B' the server has two records, 'A' and' 'B'.
My first thought was to duplicate each of ptt, rit and xit for A and B  (Main and Sub)
... but that doesn't work. .. as illustrated by the report below see below .
... j Main on Main rcvr will switch it to the sub

I haven't checked out set commands T, J and Z yet - thats another job.!

Investigation report   - Observed scope decode command sequences are consistent with behaviour.

Rcvr = Main       rigctl at command line

    RIT
	j Sub  >   stays on Main      		scope: IF;
	j Main >   switches to Sub rcvr 	scope: IF; VS0; ID; IF; VS1; ID;
                        and stays there
   PTT 	
	t Sub  >   stays on Main rcvr		scope: TX;   (TX0; returned)
	t Main >   switches to Sub rcvr		scope: IF; VS0;  ID; TX; IF;  VS1;  ID;
                        and stays there
  XIT
	z Sub  >   stays on Msain rcvr 		scope: IF;
	z Main >   switches to Sub rcvr	 	scope: IF; VS0; ID; If; VS1;  ID;j Main
                        and stays there

Rcvr = Sub      rigctl at command line

  RIT
	j Sub  >   stays on Sub   
	j Main >   flashes to Main and back to Sub    

  PTT
	t Sub  >   stays on Sub
	t Main >   flashes to Main and back to Sub

  XIT


	z Sub  >   stays on Sub
	z Main >   flashes to Main and back to Sub
		
Ian Sumner
G3VPX

[jtzMainSub.txt](https://github.com/Hamlib/Hamlib/files/5469476/jtzMainSub.txt)

title: C++ interface problems
body:
I've linked the C++ test-program `testcpp.exe` with the `Hamlib++.lib` import-library just fine. The all-DLL dependency
thus looks like:
```
testcpp.exe
  Hamlib-4++.dll
    Hamlib-4.dll
  ...
```

But when studying it's export table, I see that `testcpp.exe` exports the whole `class Rig`! 
It seems the `include/hamlib/rig_dll.h` is wrong about the `BACKEND_IMPEXP` when `IN_HAMLIB` is *not* 
defined and  `DLL_EXPORT` is defined.

I mean, in `c++/testcpp.cc`, when `DLL_EXPORT` is defined the compiler should see `class __declspec(dllimport) Rig`, no?
As it's now it sees and compiles `class __declspec(dllexport) Rig`.

But with this little patch I get want's expected (nothing exported from `testcpp.exe`):
```diff 
--- a/include/hamlib/rig_dll.h 2019-10-10 20:09:38
+++ b/include/hamlib/rig_dll.h 2021-02-26 11:27:06
@@ -56,7 +56,7 @@
 #      define BACKEND_IMPEXP HAMLIB_DLL_EXPORT
 #      define HAMLIB_IMPEXP HAMLIB_DLL_EXPORT
 #    else
-#      define BACKEND_IMPEXP HAMLIB_DLL_EXPORT
+#      define BACKEND_IMPEXP HAMLIB_DLL_IMPORT
 #      define HAMLIB_IMPEXP HAMLIB_DLL_IMPORT
 #    endif
 #  else

```

I assume these things doesn't matter on non-Windows or MinGW (with it's auto-import etc.).
But using MSVC / clang-cl, the issues with import/export is a truly mess and should be improved.

As a start, maybe rename `BACKEND_IMPEXP` to `HAMLIB_CPP_IMPEXP` perhaps. Since it's the only back-end AFAICS.

title: rigctl M PKTLSB does wierd things on KX3.
body:
Hi,

I have been trying to nail down a wierd issue in hamlib/rigctl on KX3.  I have the latest kx3 firmware 02.95 and dsp 01.52 (taken from the KX3 menu readout).   So in short I can probably provide whatever logs you might need but lacked finding it so let me know.   

So if one sets the rig to 'data rev' mode from the rigs panel rigctl is fine this way:

```
$ rigctl -m 2045 -r /dev/ttyUSB0 m
PKTLSB
2000
```

Now if we try to set it from rigctl like :

```
$ rigctl -m 2045 -r /dev/ttyUSB0 m
PKTUSB
2000
$ rigctl -m 2045 -r /dev/ttyUSB0 M PKTLSB 2000
$ rigctl -m 2045 -r /dev/ttyUSB0 m
PKTLSB
500
```

And instead of going to data rev mode it throws the rig into Data 'AFSK 45 bps' mode instead of 'DATA A' mode set to LSB.  This is commonly used for modes like RTTY or  legacy HF Packet so it'd be nice to fix this if its possible and not something maybe lost in the translation from hamlib to CAT.  It seems to work just fine in apps like win4k3suite or nap3.  Im running linux but can test those just fine over serial from a VM or WINE.

I noticed this when I was trying to write a hardware file for quisk in python but traced it back to something wierd hamlib does.  Im not sure but I thought it was fine some time ago maybe in hamlib 2 or 3.   

This is built using :
```
$ rigctl -V
rigctl Hamlib 4.2~git
Last commit was Thu Feb 25 20:05:06 2021 +0000 SHA=2a60fd

```

Not sure if it helps or not but posting this for you since Im using Manjaro and needed to test this against the latest code I modified the 'hamlib-git' AUR package to match dependancy for 'hamlib' with my PKGBUILD:

title: Mac python binding not compiling with python 3.8/3.9
body:
The Macports team has been working hard to add variants to its existing Hamlib port to add support for Python bindings for users on the Mac.

Please see:

https://trac.macports.org/ticket/62580

Here is the status of the new python bindings related variants of the Hamlib port on the Mac:
hamlib           WORKS!
hamlib+python2.7 Bindings  WORKS!
hamlib+python3.7 Bindings WORKS!
hamlib+python3.8 Bindings FAILS TO BUILD :-(
hamlib+python3.9 Bindings FAILS to BUILD :-(

The problem with the building hamlib with either Python 3.8 or Python 3.9 bindings 
appear to stem with a problem with the Hamlib configuration (configure.ac).

In particular, the problem appears to lie in the check at line ​https://github.com/Hamlib/Hamlib/blob/c6608569fcd07895d2a1a8f523b8851fd55e3957/configure.ac#L582

As a result, the compile fails:

      _SwigPyObject_own in hamlibpy_wrap.o
      __wrap_rig_debug in hamlibpy_wrap.o
.....
.....
"__Py_NotImplementedStruct", referenced from:
      _SwigPyObject_richcompare in hamlibpy_wrap.o
ld: symbol(s) not found for architecture x86_64
clang: error: linker command failed with exit code 1 (use -v to see invocation)

title: IC-821H does not switch between MAIN/SUB when calling icom_set_freq with gpredict client
body:
A Gpredict client connected to rigctld (compiled from latest github) appears to not correctly switch between Main/sub. 

The Main VFO is updated correctly according to doppler from gpredict. The sub VFO is static. verbose output from rigcltd shows 
(Note this in non-satellite mode - for the differences with satellite mode, see below)

```
icom_set_freq called currVFO=432156217.000000
icom_set_freq: special check for vfo swap
icom_set_freq: set freq failed: Command rejected by the rig
icom_set_freq: set freq failed: Command rejected by the rig
```
I have checked recent commits such as this for the ic910h:
https://github.com/Hamlib/Hamlib/issues/657

Before this commit the ic910h had special cases for cross band freq changes temporarily swapping to VFO_SUB and performing the change there. That commit removed those special cases and falls back on `icom_set_freq()`. This is the sort of thing needed forthe 821 I believe. 

However,  `821h.c` looks like it makes no attempt to handle these cases. But it seems the 821 config does not trigger the "special" behaviour in `icom_set_freq()` .

I have the C knowledge, but lack familiarity with the code. I have the radio sitting on my desk, newly acquired. 

Rather than hack something, if I could be given some guidance on best way to trigger to the MAIN/SUB swap for set_freq on other band, then I should be able to create a pull request.  

Thanks

title: rigctl and rigctld need to try to reopen rig when an error occurs

labels.name: Needs test
labels.description: Patches have been submitted but need testing to close issue

labels.name: Critical
labels.description: A problem for common operations with WSJT-X, GPredict, RigPi, etc.

body:
Right now rigctl/rigctld does not try to reopen the rig when a rig error occurs.
Commented out the reopen attempt as it was the incorrect way to do it and was causing problems with PiWeb.
So now running "rigctld -m 4" for example will no longer reconnect if the network connection to FLRig aborts for any reason.
rigctl and rigctld should both attempt to reconnect to network or serial devices when a hard device error occurs but should return an error and simply try to reconnect on each command.
e.g.
rigctl -r com3 
f (error occurs because serial port reset -- should attempt a re-open a couple of times)
if reopen does not succed return error
f (again tries to reopen rig)
f (again tried to reopen rig)

So hamlib will do 3 reopen attempts with a 1 second wait between each and hopefully succeed.  If not will return error and on next command will do 3 open attempts again....ad nauseum.

title: FTdx101D RFPOWER_METER_WATTS range

labels.name: Needs test
labels.description: Patches have been submitted but need testing to close issue

body:
The RF power setting range of the FTdx101D is 5w - 100w
\get_level Main RFPOWER correctly returns 0.050 to 1.000

However, the power meter should have range 0 - 100+
but in rigctl it  has range 5 to 100+ 

The power meter scale on the rig is non quite linear 0 - 150w and the value returned from RM5; appears
to be the linear position on the scale 0 -255
So rigctl does a good calibration job, as its return of 5- 100 accurately matches the scale.
It IS actually displaying the output (not the control)   ... because if I switch from dummy load
to no load the value returned from \get_level VFOA RFPOWER_METER_WATTS drops from 100 to 26.8
- exactly as the meter on the rig.

The problem is the lower limit of 5w which applies to the control but not to RM5; measured output power.

So  when I switch to transmit on SSB with no modulation, the rig's power meter correctly shows zero
but the rigctl CAT derived meter shows 5w - which loos as if I have bad carrier suppression problem.
At  this time,   \send_cmd_rx RM5; 10   correctly returns RM5000000;  = 0w

Ian
G3VPX

title: IC7000 \set_mode does not set bandwidth

labels.name: Needs test
labels.description: Patches have been submitted but need testing to close issue

body:
Similar to issue #496 

Problem  IC7000 \set_mode LSB 2800 only sets mode (not passband)
\get_mode then always reports a default for the mode (SSB 2000,  CW 350) 

\set_mode LSB 2800 works fine on FTdx101D
--------------------------------------------------
Observation on scope decode:

**\set_mode USB 2700**    decode

rigctl sends: FE FE 70 E0 06 01 FD    rig response is   FE FE E0 70 FB FD (ok)
then
nothing else - no passband setting

Mode setting is correct - sets USB  with code 01
-----------------------------------------------
\get_mode has no problem.
eg: with rig  set to mode = CW and bw = 350
**\get_mode**    decode

rigctl sends: FE FE 70 E0 04 FD   rig response is:   FE FE E0 70 04 03 20 FD
then
rigctl sends: FE FE 70 E0 1A 03 FD  rig response is: FE FE E0 70 1A 03 06 FD

this is correct and displays  CW  350 Hz

Ian Sumner
G3VPX

body:
Running piWebCAT:  Main: LSB  3000Hz    Sub CW-U 1400Hz
Main selected. 
    piWebaCAT configured to do a \get_mode Main and a \get_mode Sub every 1-2 seconds

I observe:  LSB button illuminated - but flips to CW and back every 2 seconds or so

I cannot reproduce this with telnet, but after much trying to prove otherwise
I think it is in rigctld
Reason for this:    String read from socket as: "CW\n3000\n"
                                  I can't be generating this?  CW is Sub mode.  3000 is Main BW.
Form web browser inspect element > network listing I see:

\get_mode Sub   >   CW\n1400\n        = ok        Sub mode and Sub BW
\get_mode Main   >  CW\n3000\n       = wrong  Sub mode and Main BW

If I switch off the background check of \get_mode Sub

title: IC-9700 VFOs incorrect

labels.name: Needs test
labels.description: Patches have been submitted but need testing to close issue

body:
IC-9700 VFOs seem a bit confused.  In hamlib's abstraction:
1st VFO has MainA and MainB
2nd VFO has SubA and SubB
In Sat mode MainA and SubA are active and MainB/SubB return errors.  Main/Sub calls should map to MainA/SubA
In non-Sat mode 1st VFO Main/Sub should map to MainA/MainB -- this would be WSJT-X split ops for example
In non-Sat mode 2nd VFO active Main/Sub should map to SubA/SubB -- not sure how this would be used but would be consistent

title: LIBUSB problem

labels.name: Needs test
labels.description: Patches have been submitted but need testing to close issue

labels.name: Critical
labels.description: A problem for common operations with WSJT-X, GPredict, RigPi, etc.

body:
it looks like the above commit causes critical libusb code to be #ifdef
excluded, I am seeing this on MS Windows MinGW builds. The configuration
macro HAVE_LIBUSB_H is being used and that is not defined, perhaps
HAVE_LIBUSB_1_0_LIBUSB_H should have been used? Offending code is at
src/iofunc.c lines 149 and 206. Also src/rotator.c lines 64, 421, and 533.

73
Bill
G4WJS.

title: Add get_rig_info function

labels.name: Needs test
labels.description: Patches have been submitted but need testing to close issue

body:
Add get_rig_info to return satellite mode, and RX TX flags for each VFO
Examples:
Normal non-split ops
VFO=VFOA Freq=10133000 Mode=LSB Width=0 RX=1 TX=1
VFOB Freq=10134000 Mode= LSB Width=0 RX=0 TX=0
Split=0 SatMode=0
Or
VFO=Main Freq=10133000 Mode=LSB Width=0 RX=1 TX=1
VFO=Sub Freq=10134000 Mode=LSB Width=0 RX=0 TX=0
Split=0 SatMode=0

In split mode -- 9700 for example uses VFOA/B in split mode
VFO=VFOA Freq=10133000 Mode=LSB Width=0 RX=1 TX=0
VFO=VFOB Freq=10134000 Mode=LSB Width=0 RX=0 TX=1
Split=1 SatMode=0

In satellite mode -- 9700 for examples uses Main/Sub in sat mode
VFO=Main Freq=10133000 Mode=LSB Width=0 RX=1 TX=0
VFO=Sub Freq=10134000 Mode=LSB Width=0 RX=0 TX=1
Split=0 SatMode=1

VFOB is active
VFO=VFOA Freq=10133000 Mode=LSB Width=0 RX=0 TX=0
VFO=VFOB Feq=10134000 Mode=LSB Width=0 RX=1 TX=1
Split=0 SatMode=0

Would also show reverse split or reverse uplink/downlink in satmode if supported.
VFO=VFOA Freq=10133000 Mode=LSB Width=0 RX=0 TX=1
VFO=VFOB Feq=10134000 Mode=LSB Width=0 RX=1 TX=0
Split=1 SatMode=0

title: Kenwood rit not working

labels.name: Needs test
labels.description: Patches have been submitted but need testing to close issue

body:
Mike

Me again, and again RIT. A friend asked me to look at hamlib and RIT on
the TS2000, as it appeared to be a bit odd.

I agree with him - Hamlib follows what the spec APPEARS to say, but I
think the spec is wrong.

For RD and RU, P1 says 00000-99999 (The offset frequency in Hz)

What it appears to actually DO is to apply that offset to the RIT as an
increment.

Attached output from a rigctl run.

I'd fix it and send a pull request, but I suspect the problem applies
to ALL Kenwood rigs, and the TS2000 is the only one I have access to.

Mike G0GJV

title: Bandwith problem IC-705
body:
Hi,

When requesting bandwidth of IC-705 through rig_passband_narrow, rig_passband_normal and rig_passband_wide, results in 0, 2.4 and 3.6 (maybe not in that exact order).
Changing ic7300.c for the ic705 capabilities struct (filters part) to 

    .filters =  {
        {RIG_MODE_SSB | RIG_MODE_PKTLSB | RIG_MODE_PKTUSB, kHz(2.4)},
        {RIG_MODE_SSB | RIG_MODE_PKTLSB | RIG_MODE_PKTUSB, kHz(1.8)},
        {RIG_MODE_SSB | RIG_MODE_PKTLSB | RIG_MODE_PKTUSB, kHz(3)},
        {RIG_MODE_CW | RIG_MODE_CWR | RIG_MODE_RTTY | RIG_MODE_RTTYR, Hz(500)},
        {RIG_MODE_CW | RIG_MODE_CWR | RIG_MODE_RTTY | RIG_MODE_RTTYR, Hz(250)},
        {RIG_MODE_CW | RIG_MODE_CWR, kHz(1.2)},
        {RIG_MODE_RTTY | RIG_MODE_RTTYR, kHz(2.4)},
        {RIG_MODE_AM | RIG_MODE_PKTAM, kHz(6)},
        {RIG_MODE_AM | RIG_MODE_PKTAM, kHz(3)},
        {RIG_MODE_AM | RIG_MODE_PKTAM, kHz(9)},
        {RIG_MODE_FM | RIG_MODE_PKTFM, kHz(10)},
        {RIG_MODE_FM | RIG_MODE_PKTFM, kHz(7)},
        {RIG_MODE_FM | RIG_MODE_PKTFM, kHz(15)},
        RIG_FLT_END,
    },
fixes this. Do not know why this was implemented different for the IC-705 as 3.6KHz is not one of the standard filters.

Kind regards,

Wim.

title: grig shows empty dropdowns for ATT and PREAMP w/ FUNCube Dongle ProPlus (rigs/kit/funcube.c)
body:
grig cannot control LNA or mixer gain due to empty dropdowns for ATT and PREAMP w/ FUNCube Dongle ProPlus (funcube.c)
Caused by funcubeplus_caps having no attenuator and preamp fields defined.

Currently, the LNA's on/off is mapped to PREAMP as 0 or 1 and the mixer gain's on/off is mapped to ATT as 0 or 1. The FCDPP's mixer gain is pretty consistently 20dB when enabled. The LNA's gain varies between 15dB to 5dB up the tuning range. There are a few ways I could go about making the FCDPP LNA and Mixer controllable over grig:

* Add funcubeplus_caps.preamp[] with a value of 1 in its array and funcubeplus_caps.attenuator[] with a value of 1 in its array for the mixer gain. This is the most backwards compatible to the original behavior, but grig shows the PREAMP option as 1dB and ATT option as -1dB.
* Add funcubeplus_caps.preamp[] with a value of 10 in its array to approximate the gain of the LNA and  funcubeplus_caps.attenuator[] with a value of 20 for the mixer gain, then change RIG_LEVEL_ATT switch case to disable Mixer Gain when set to 20, else enable Mixer Gain when set to 0. This would not be backwards compatible to the previous behavior.
* Merge both Mixer Gain and LNA as values in PREAMP by listing all permutations of the LNA and PREAMP on/off states such that:  0dB = (LNAoff, MixGainOff), 10dB = (LNAon, MixGainOff), 20dB= (LNAoff, MixGainOn), 30dB = (LNAon, MixGainOn), then discard the ATT level capability. This is not backwards compatible, but is logically the closest to actual behavior without losing any control.
* Leave it alone.

Which would you prefer?

title: CM108: unable to trigger default pin setting because I can't see a way to set rig port to CM108

labels.name: Needs test
labels.description: Patches have been submitted but need testing to close issue

body:
In order to correctly trigger the PTT on a modified CM108 chip that has been attached to GPIO3, we need to use `ptt_bitnum = 2`, which makes sense as a default and it looks like this is the intention of the [code](https://github.com/Hamlib/Hamlib/blob/b0e006ce6cdf1262938abd581d9d25f1df96cfe9/src/rig.c#L443):

``` c
#  define DEFAULT_CM108_PTT_BITNUM 2
```

``` c
   switch (caps->port_type)
    {
    // [...]
    case RIG_PORT_CM108:
        strncpy(rs->rigport.pathname, DEFAULT_CM108_PORT, HAMLIB_FILPATHLEN);
        rs->rigport.parm.cm108.ptt_bitnum = DEFAULT_CM108_PTT_BITNUM;
        rs->pttport.parm.cm108.ptt_bitnum = DEFAULT_CM108_PTT_BITNUM;
        break;
```

However, this is only triggered if the `port_type` is set to `RIG_PORT_CM108`, but I can't see any way to do this:

```
$ rg RIG_PORT_CM108
include/hamlib/rig.h:    RIG_PORT_CM108,         /*!< CM108 GPIO */
src/iofunc.c:    case RIG_PORT_CM108:
src/rig.c:    case RIG_PORT_CM108:
```

The enum value seems to be defined but not used anywhere.

It is simple to workaround the issue by explicitly setting the bitnum on the command line:

```
$ rigctl -L -C ptt_bitnum=2 -P CM108
```

but the code does seem to suggest that this setting should be the default.

Should a model of the dummy rig be added that sets the port to `RIG_PORT_CM108`, or is there a place for another rig to be added that has this setting?

I've been using WSJT-X plus JTAlert quite happily for some time now.

Lately I noticed that as I change bands with WSJT-X that the antennas were not changing as set up, Menu item 31 set to BAND.

I'm not saying the rig file is broken as I haven't seen anyone else bringing this to light on the Groups.io site.

title: Allow using two separate rotator models for Az/El
body: This is a bit related to #747, where a Green Heron rotator controller has separate serial ports for Az and El control. In addition to this, I think Hamlib could provide an abstraction over two completely separate rotators/models where one of them would control azimuth and another elevation. Basically most (all?) Hamlib client software seems to assume that a single rotator handles both azimuth and elevation rotation, so if one has two separate rotators and separate controllers for both azimuth and elevation, using them as one unit is not easy (or possible at all).

labels.description: Patches have been submitted but need testing to close issue

Regression from older hamlib.
Every time the FreeDV Start button is pressed the rig selects VFOA.
This results from the patch for this issue
https://github.com/Hamlib/Hamlib/issues/745
So we will change to only set VFOA on the 1st rig_open.

title: FreeDV with TS-890 always selects VFOA with hamlib 4.3, VFOB usable with hamlib 4.2
body:

FreeDV is used with a Kenwood TS-890

title: What is the intended use case of rig_cookie?
body:
I think I understand what rig_cookie is trying to achieve: implement some sort of locking to allow multi-threaded applications.
But I think there are some serious issues;

1. Locking is only done when having pthread, so if that is not enabled there is no multi thread guarantee.
2. Even if pthread is available the lock should also be used when reading cookie to protect against writes, not just when setting.
3. The lock should also protect timestamp.
4. Fetching timestamp should be done AFTER getting the lock. otherwise significant time could have past waiting for the lock.

To me it really seems like a problem that should be solved at the application layer. Why is hamlib trying to provide this? Are there any known users?

title: What is the policy on checking for rig for the rig back end
body:
I was wondering about the assumption a rig back end can make on the rig pointer being `!null`.
I see some code that assume `rig != NULL`, while other code adds actual checks. Either not checking is a bug or checking is redundant.

Running a simple grep on check for rig pointer not being NULL:
`grep -R '!rig[^_-]' --include=*.[ch] rigs`
shows most older Yaesu rigs have checks for every possible function, most other rigs have no check or only one. Most check only in the close function.

I think all these check are (no longer?) required. I expect these should only be accessed via the API which could check this.

RPRT 0

14220000
m currVFO

3000

RPRT 0
m currVFO               <------- currVFO is still OK.
AM
9000
f currVFO

m VFOB                <-----but the VFOB, that is current (in rig's display) shows now VFOA (that is behind) freq and mode via rigctld
CW
500
f VFOB
14220000

AM
9000
f VFOA
3750000


In words:
When rig display shows vfoA and rigctld commands are used to switch first to vfoB (that comes to display) and then change mode then currVFO still shows same mode and freq what rig's display but when asking via VFOA and/or VFOB the contents get mixed upside down.

So it seems that to get always correct mode and frequency with all rigs, including icoms that can not report vfo, only "currVFO" at first parameter can be trusted.
VFOA and VFOB may work with rigs that can report vfo properly (I can not test that here).

title: TS-890S VFOB problem

labels.name: Needs test
labels.description: Patches have been submitted but need testing to close issue

body:
as a follow up, a WSJT-X user reports incorrect split VFO behaviour on this rig. I have tracked it down to starting with VFO B selected as the current VFO before starting Hamlib, if VFO A is selected as the current VFO Hamlib behaves. This rig is one of many where VFO A and VFO B has identical functionality and Hamlib should not care which is selected when it is started. Here are two trace logs, the first starting with VFO B as current, the second with VFO A as current:

https://www.dropbox.com/s/x4esf0nh58z6e6r/WSJT-X_RigControl-TS-890s-VFOB.log?dl=1

https://www.dropbox.com/s/ikz77duzpd04spv/WSJT-X_RigControl-TS-890s-VFOA.log?dl=1

The misbehaviour is that the split Tx VFO does not change when a frequency change is requested via rig_set_split_freq_mode(), instead Hamib always changes VFO B, even when the Tx VFO is supposed to be VFO A. This trace line seems to be the root of the issue:

[2021-07-18 13:36:08.510887][00:00:15.531727][RIGCTRL:trace] vfo_fixup: RIG_VFO_TX changed to VFOB, split=1, satmode=0
73
Bill
G4WJS.

title: TS-2000 doppler problem

labels.name: Needs test
labels.description: Patches have been submitted but need testing to close issue

labels.name: Critical
labels.description: A problem for common operations with WSJT-X, GPredict, RigPi, etc.

body:
I was having a CAT rig control problem relating to trying to change Tx frequency while transmitting. I noticed this when running on 10GHz. I had not previously noticed it when running on 1296MHz. I am not sure whether the issue has always been there, and I didn't notice it because the Doppler changes are much less frequent on 1296, or whether this has only become an issue with the latest release of WSJT-X.
 
I know others have had issues with using the TS2000 - so I hope this helps some.
 
Set up:
TS200 with firmware version 11 (previously noted that versions prior to 9 had CAT control problems) WSJT-X v2.5.1
 
I had problems with the following settings:
1) The option "Allow Tx frequency changes while transmitting" ticked
2) Split operation "Rig"(and the TS2000 in split mode)
 
With these settings, when transmitting the TS2000 would show a Doppler correction when transmitting, but then stop with the error box indicating rig control problem.
 
The error message was:
Hamlib error: Command rejected by the rig
Kenwood.c(577):kenwood_transaction return (-9)
Kenwood.c(1350):kenwood_set_split_vfo return (-9)
Rig.c(4658):rig_set_split_vfo return (-9) while setting split mode
 
I could click "Retry" and it would then run again until the next Doppler correction, when the error would repeat.
 
If I unticked the "Allow Tx frequency changes while transmitting" there would be no crashes, but of course also no frequency corrections during the transmit period
 
The following seems to have sorted the problem:
1)  The option "Allow Tx frequency changes while transmitting" ticked
2) Split operation "Fake it" (and the TS2000 of course in simplex mode)
 
Now, Doppler correction occurs during the transmit (and receive) periods and no crashes.
 
The basic cure, as suggested to me by Charlie, G3WDG, appears to be the change from Split Rig to Fake it.
 
 
So everything now seems fine for JT65/Q65, but will be doing further testing with CW.
 
73
David, G4YTL

title: power2mW buffer overflow
body:
I saw this issue described in a tweet: https://twitter.com/JeffSipek/status/1457167104600383488

Here's the content:

TIL that hamlib uses sprintf in its netrigctl code.  If I try to get the power (via rig_power2mW) and specify a frequency with more than 7 decimal digits (IOW >9.999999 MHz), it overflows the command buffer. macOS catches this somehow and kills the process 

The format string is:

“\\power2mW %f %.0f %s\n”

The first %f produces: 0.250000
The second: 14230000
The %s: USB

For a total of 32 bytes written to a: char cmdbuf[32];

title: IC-910 not changing modes
body: When using GPredict with hamlib, the IC-910 does not change modes (USB, LSB, FM) when using the radio control feature. (This menu is in the upper right corner of main window.)  Is this a hamlib issue or a GPredict issue?  I am using hamlib-w64-4.3.1.exe

title: rotctl dummy not emulating timing
body:
It is maybe over year since I have last played with rotctld. Using rotor
Dummy #1 is a good second choice as there are not so many rotors to test
with.

If I do remember right issuing P or M command has made Dummy to "turn"
slowly so that one can see what happens with CO program while polling
rigctld.
At the moment (rotctl(d), Hamlib 4.4~git su marras 07 14:21:54 2021
+0000 SHA=41ebbb) issuing P or M causes Dummy to jump immediately to
given position, or to end of turn. With M the speed value seems to be
useless, too (actually I do not remember did it ever work) but P did
cause slowly changing reading.

Is this delay loop removed in purpose from Dummy rotator?

--
Saku
OH1KH

title: Kenwood split allow either direction
body:
Kenwood split mode is currently fixed to RX=VFOA TX=VFOB.  Also uses the IF command to retrieve split vfo which is bogus for which VFO is actually selected for RX/TX.
So need to change to using FR/FT to set/retrieve the actual VFO and the ptt status to determine the current vfo while transmitting.

Finish implementing ENTER and RETRUINFUNC macros to replace enter debug statement and return statements in all code.
This allow a single location to change the message format for each for future enhancements.

title: Support transceiver polling on Windows
body:
It looks like polling needs sigaction() to exist on Windows to function properly if [this](https://github.com/Hamlib/Hamlib/blob/master/src/event.c#L225) is any indication. Unfortunately, it does not, hence why the feature disables itself. Any possibility of porting that functionality over from Unix/Linux?

(This issue came up during the submission of [this PR](https://github.com/drowe67/freedv-gui/pull/47) for another project. The feature seemed to work on Mac and Linux but not Windows.)

title: Implement always use cache

title: Find a workaround to get Icom VFO state to properly support Icom transceive data
body:
Follow-up task for features initially implemented in #892.

Icom transceive data doesn't contain any information about the current VFO, so it is not possible to use it to update Hamlib cache state on its own.

However, we could probably find some clever way to use the 0x25 CI-V command to figure out which VFO is currently active.

It seems that at least IC-7300 outputs a mode change transceive message when changing VFO (even if the mode doesn't change), so that could be potentially used as a trigger to execute the logic to figure out the current VFO.

title: "w64" exe file is actually 32-bit
body:
Upon downloading https://github.com/Hamlib/Hamlib/releases/download/4.4/hamlib-w64-4.4.exe and initiating the installation, I saw that it wanted to install into C:\Program Files(x86)\..., which made me suspicious. I aborted the install and checked the properties of hamlib-w64-4.4.exe using the steps outlined at https://www.digitalcitizen.life/3-ways-learn-whether-windows-program-64-bit-or-32-bit/, method 3. Specifically, when choosing the Compatibility Mode, Windows 95 was the first option, so I concluded that the subject file was 32-bit, though its name implied 64-bit.

Workaround: I downloaded https://github.com/Hamlib/Hamlib/releases/download/4.4/hamlib-w32-4.4.zip and unzipped it. At least hamlib-w64-4.4/bin/rigctl.exe is 64-bit, as tested by the same method as above. I have not tested all of the executables.

title: QSX TS-440 Audio does not work TS-480 Audio works
body:
Finished my QDX Rev. 2. and had a hard time to run it :-(

I use JTDX on my (Dell 13") laptop, because JTDX shows twice the number of FT4/FT8 decodes,
compared to WSJT-X, on the left screen. That makes sense on a laptop to see more..
But the QDX blinked twice with two blinks and stopped TX. Same if I tried the 'Tune' button.

Setting was TS-440S, it is the 440 with an 'S', there is no TS-440' to be selected. Looks like, that's
the latest implementation of hamlib. There was no way, even after setting in QDX via serial terminal
'Configuration' the 'Audio Gain' from 5000 up to 9999. No way ;-( It looked all the time, that the QDX
wanted to tell me with 2 x blink = your audio level is low.

But did not give up, why not select TS-480 as the rig ? - done - QDX does not not blink / complain
anymore! All is fine! Have no idea what the difference in CAT control (if there is any) makes this happen.

===

Remark: 'Audio Gain' is back to default setting 5000 in the QDX. Just TS-480 as the rig.


73 de Wolfgang
OE1MWW

title: Expand data types accepted by XML-RPC
body:
I'm writing my own Flrig-like application that can communicate with Hamlib (using the Flrig rig) and Fldigi via XML-RPC. I'm writing it in Python using the [xmlrpc.server](https://docs.python.org/3/library/xmlrpc.server.html) module. This module doesn't support the `nil` or `i4` data types, but it [does support](https://docs.python.org/3/library/xmlrpc.client.html) `int` and `string`.

I've found that by changing this line in Hamlib's `rigs/dummy/flrig.c`:

```
    if (streq(p, "i4") || streq(p, "double"))
```
to:
```
    if (streq(p, "i4") || streq(p, "double") || streq(p, "int") || streq(p, "string"))
```
that my application works well with Hamlib. It already works well with Fldigi without modifications to Fldigi.

Would you consider making this change in your source code?

title: Yaesu Band select
body:
Implement Band select command in Yaesu newcat backend. It is useful beacuse it allows to use the Yaesu stack function.
I suggest to add this command as level in the set_level function.

Command format is:
BS P1P1;

Where P1P1 is integer

Yaesu FT991 example:
00 - 1.8 MHz
01 - 3.5 MHz
02 - 5
03 - 7
04 - 10
05 - 14
06 - 18
07 - 21
08 - 24.5
09 - 28
10 - 50
11 - GEN
12 - MW
13 - not used
14 - AIR
15 - 144 MHz
16 - 430

title: DNS lookup on connect causes delay
body:
It appears when a connection comes in to rigctld it performs a reverse loopup of the source address. Depending on circumstance this can cause quite a delay.

In this case rigctld is running on a Windows 11 box and is being queried from a Pi over the local network.

For example:

```
pi@rpi4:~/tools $ time ./get_rigctl.sh 192.168.9.25 52222 f
14173000

real    0m4.679s
user    0m0.000s
sys     0m0.008s
```

That's nearly 5 seconds in this case. I can see in the rigctl output:

```
Connection opened from rpi4:36714
...
...
Connection closed from rpi4:36714
```
The delay occurs before the `Connection opened` line is outputted. This all suggests it it is indeed performing some kind of DNS related shinanigans in order to resolve it as 'rpi4'.  Having looked at the available options (-L) I don't see any mention of being able to disable these lookups.

I can also see the PTR lookup hitting the local nameserver (answered in 1.3ms):

```
2021-11-20 12:37:23 | PTR | 35.9.168.192.in-addr.arpa | ROCKET.local | OK INSECURE | DOMAIN (1.3ms)
```
This lookup only hits the nameserver after this weird random delay so I'm confused what it's doing before making this PTR DNS request as that's the bit that's taking all the time. Maybe it's not DNS causing the delay but something is as I've no idea what.

If I use different software which also has a rigctld compatible interface (namely SparkSDR) there's no delay whatsoever so it's specific to rigctld.

My questions are therefore:

1) Does the ability to disable lookup already exist?
2) Could it be implemented?
3) Is there a simple change I could make and recompile it myself to test?

Thanks

labels.name: Critical
labels.description: A problem for common operations with WSJT-X, GPredict, RigPi, etc.

body:
I'm using Windows 11 with Quisk v4.1.93 and Hermes Lite 2 SDR TCVR with hamlib-w64-4.4.

WSJT-X v2.4.0 worked well and synchronized with Quisk in less than 1 second when initially started and less than 1 second when changing band and frequency.
WSJT-X v2.5.2 takes 15 second to synchronize with Quisk when initially started and then less than 1 second when changing band and frequency, the "?" indicator turns green.
WSJT-X v2.5.3 and 2.5.4 do not synchronize with Quisk using the same hamlib and CAT parameters, The "?" indicator right to the band selector turns orange/red and in the "settings" menu the "Test CAT" button turns RED when actuated.

I already posted twice explaining that. Some members suggested to replace the libhamlib-4.dll file in the program Bin folder, which I did without success, the reason why I reverted to v2.5.2 after testing 2.5.3 and 2.5.4.
73 - Pierre - FK8IH

I hadn't looked at wsjtx_syslog.log in a few weeks ( since upgrade from 2.5.3 to 2.5.4 )
Today I noticed that the log contains RIGCTL warning message for each FT8 cycle.

 [RIGCTRL][2022-01-17 20:08:10.565987][04:16:35.503896][warning] kenwood_get_split_vfo_if(1583): unknown rxVFO=None

Despite fact that there is a warning, everything seems to be operating normally. The warnings did not occur in  2.5.3.

I have wsjt-x configured to use Flex 6xxx as rig type and split set to None.

title: Commands via API always seem to use VFO mode
body:

I'm trying to remotely control an SDR software (https://github.com/AlexandreRouma/SDRPlusPlus) that implements a rigctld compatible backend but without VFO mode.

I can connect and send commands just fine with rigctl, as you can see it sends the right command:

`Rigctl command: 'F 146000000.000000'`

title: FT-991A - "Communication bus collision" error when tuning VHF/UHF
body:
I was manually sending some commands to rigctl and got a "Communication bus collision error" when trying to tune the radio: 

```
> rigctl.exe  -m 1035 -r COM3 U TUNER 2
set_func: error = Communication bus collision
newcat.c(10331):newcat_set_cmd return(-14)
newcat.c(5649):newcat_set_func return(-14)
rigctl_parse.c(3312):rigctl_set_func return(-14)

After a little messing around I realized I accidentally moved to 2 meters, which you can't run the antenna tuner on.

title: FT5000 band stack
body:
https://jtdx.freeforums.net/thread/72/jtdx2-2-159-changes-mode?page=1&scrollTo=370

I have found that while running JTDX if an interesting spot appears on the Cluster and I use the Bandstack option in the FT5000 to move me to the SSB part of the band, (on each band I have it set for FT8 frequency, SSB section and one for the CW end of the bands), I used to be able to check if I could hear the DX without having to close JTDX. If I didn't hear the DX I just pressed the Band button again to move back to the FT8 frequency and continue with FT8.

What I have noticed now is that using the same process under 159 when I go to the CW section to check if I can hear the DX spotted 159 changes the mode to USB! this didn't happen in 156 and I have gone back to make sure and 156 sits quite happily on CW with JTDX open as long as I want to stay there listening. 

I assume something has changed in the new version, to make the mode change that wasn't happening in 156.

Is this design or a bug?

it was very useful just to be able to do a quick QSY to the CW section to check the DX without having to close JTDX.

Thanks

73
Pete
