FT-991A MD1 and ST commands
body:
When running WSJT-X with FT-991a it passes CAT TEST and PTT Test however when operating the radio and monitoring the serial port, I see MD1; command sent to the device.  This command is not a valid CAT command for the device.

My application, which monitors commands and sends to RIG sees a ? response which I do not pass back to WSJT-X.

This happens when pressing "Tune" button and when responding to CQ messages.

Prior to v2.5.4 this was not an issue.    I've also seen extraneous "ST;" commands sent as well.

title: Yaesu FT-991 AGC value
body:
According to caps dump for Yaesu FT-991 the value for AGC levels are: 0=OFF 1=SUPERFAST 2=FAST 3=SLOW 4=USER 5=MEDIUM 6=AUTO, but it's wrong.
The allowed AGC value for FT-991 (generally for newcat backend) should be: 0=OFF 2=FAST 3=SLOW 5=MEDIUM 6=AUTO, the others are not supported.

Consider also that the Yaesu "GT" command returns the exact AGC value when in AUTO: AUTO-FAST, AUTO-MEDIUM, AUTO-SLOW, but these values are not supported in the hamlib backend, it's a possible future enhancement.

body:
I got WSJT-X 2.5.4 and it sets freq and PTT's fine. But I think you may be using the wrong CI-V PTT command for the sound card.

They should be: 

fefe8ae0 1a 37 0002 fd : for PTT ON
fefe8ae0 1a 37 0000 fd : for PTT OFF

I cannot find "37" in any of the icom source files like icom.h, icom_defs.h or icf8101.c.

What happens when using the old std 1c 00 and 1c 01 is that  you get PTT but it is routing the audio via the mic I believe.  To get the audio from the USB sound card, you have to use the ones above.

Verified that FLDIGI with my RigCAT file for the radio functions normally, but WSJT-X and Direwolf give me what sounds an awful lot like feedback (which makes sense).

Let me know if I can make source adjustments here and recompile to test.  I am just not sure where to make any relevant changes.

title: K4 repeating TQ indefinitely

labels.name: Priority
labels.description: High priority for enhancement or fix but not critical

body:
Here is what is happening:
Press (accidentally) AF REC on the K4
Try to transmit with WSJT-X (e.g., via the TUNE button)
WSJT-X sends a TX; command (because of PTT via CAT)
Because the K4 is in AF REC mode (not fully implemented yet), it ignores the TX; command, and stays in receive mode
WSJT-X keeps sending TQ; commands waiting for a response (are we in transmit yet?)
The answer will always be "No" (TQ0;) until you tap XMIT or close a footswitch, then it will be "yes" (TQ1;) and all is well
It doesn't happen when using PTT via RTS because there is no TX; command sent or ignored.

title: Add lock_mode capability
body:
Certain conditions create the need to prevent other clients from changing mode.
For example, using Log4OM cluster spotting and and IC-7300 running CW Skimmer in FM mode.  Clicking on a spot in Log4OM will incorrectly set VFOA mode to CW.  But CW Skimmer is in FM mode and VFOB is CW mode.
So...the scripts to switch to CW skimmer can request "set_lock_mode 1" and all mode set commands will be ignored.
Then when CWSkimmer stops "set_lock_mode 0" will release the lock. "get_lock_mode" will return current lock status.

https://github.com/Hamlib/Hamlib/blob/0373846f8b2c8832863849bf4641a94a60cdad18/rigs/tentec/orion.c#L661

This is causing issue with 599 Eagle. This rig is kind of specific in terms of setting the bandwidth. Once the bandwidth is set via CAT command *RFxx the bandwidth knob on the front panel stops working until next power up or issuing *RF0 command. However, such command is never sent from cqrlog and perhaps other SW.

More elegant solution would be:
1. create tt599_set_mode function as a copy of tt565_set_mode
2. register tt599_set_mode to TT599 rig structure in orion.h
3. replace the quoted line with:
_SNPRINTF(mdbuf, sizeof(mdbuf), "*R%cM%c" EOM "*R%cF%d" EOM **"*R%cF0" EOM**,
             ttreceiver,
             ttmode,
             ttreceiver,
             (int)width,
             **ttreceiver**
            );_
and inrease mdbuf size by few bytes.

The outcome would be:
1. The bandwidth can be normally set via CAT command and stays set till the bandwidth button is left untouched.
2. Once the bandwidth button on the front panel is rotated it takes over the bandwidth settings (same as for setting VFO).

title: TT599 - seg fault when getting SWR reading

labels.name: Needs test
labels.description: Patches have been submitted but need testing to close issue

body:
```
$ /usr/local/bin/rigctl -m 16013 -r /dev/ttyACM0 

Rig command: \get_level SWR
Segmentation fault
```


The format of the command is quite different between Orion 565 and Eagle 599. The SWR is not calculated by the 599 radio. For Eagle 599:

`@STF<fwd watts>R<ref watts*10><CR>`

```
?S<CR> 
@STF99R10<cr>      99 watts forward, 1.0 watt reflected
```

The conversion causes segmentation fault here:
` val->f = atof(strchr(lvlbuf + 5, 'S') + 1) / 256.0;`


I guess for 599 fwd watts and ref watts must be read and SWR calculated by the driver: 
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/48401450/172612086-c64a82e0-b921-4195-9eb9-ba769dad30a7.png)


See: http://www.tentec.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/05/tt_599_program_ref_v1.001.pdf 

https://github.com/Hamlib/Hamlib/blob/24c18938c284300ff4cab7a1b516058dffa4de36/rigs/tentec/orion.c#L1296

title: multiple rig_init() calls  fail with different models
body:
I have found that in Hamlib 4.4 multiple calls to rig_init() do not work if the model type is different. For example:

```
RIG *rig1 = rig_init(2010);
RIG *rig2 = rig_init(1022);

```
`rig1` will be valid, but `rig2` will be NULL. If the model number is the same for both calls, `rig1` and `rig2` will both be valid.

The failed call gets down into `rig_caps()` in register.c where it fails to find a `rig_caps` value.

This was not an issue for Hamlib 3.3.

title: KLog wsjtx-2.6.0-RC4 problems
body:
Testing wsjtx-2.6.0-RC4 with hamlib-4.4.2 works fine, until klog-2.2.1 is running.
All seems fine initially until the end of a transmit frame, when the VFO starts to cycle, reversing TX/RX modes every second (approx).
This is with klog in read only mode for hamlib.
Rig is Kenwood TS450S.
OK, testing with wsjtx-2.5.4 there is no sign of the problem, so despite klog 'exposing' the issue, it does appear to be a change in wsjtx-2.6.0 that is causing it.
Note that in both cases wsjtx is built to use the system hamlib-4.4.2.
It seems there is a klog issue with hamlib 4.5. It does work, as I tested with wsjtx-2.6.0 above, however the hamlib test button in settings remains red and when pressed it locks up klog. (Without wsjtx running and using rigctld).

title: Debug tracing
body:
See if we can provide a "level" indication in the debug messages to show the function call depth.  Would make reviewing the debug info easier to trace.

So level 1 at top and each level down would increment by 1 on entry and decrement by 1 on exit.
This can probably be done via the ENTERFUNC and RETURNFUNC.  But RETURNFUNC may be called without an associated ENTERFUNC and vice versa so a state machine will be needed to determine when to increment/decrement.
ENTERFUNC would be if (state==RETURNFUNC) ++depth
RETURNFUNC would be if (state == ENTERRFUNC) ++ depth
ENTERFUNC would set ENTERFUNC state
RETURNFUNC would set RETURNFUNC state
get_depth function/macro would return depth when state==ENTERFUNC and depth+1 when state==RETURNFUNC
ENTERFUNC would only increment depth if state==RETURNFUNC
RETURNFUNC would only decrement depth if state==ENTERFUNC

title: Display frequency does not match get_freq - TS-950SDX
body:
# Problem

When `rigctl` connects to Kenwood TS-950SDX the frequency from the information readout `IF` matches the displayed frequency on the radio, but in contrast when `FA` or `FB` (`get_freq`) is issued the response does not match the displayed frequency. `set_freq` does not set the frequency on the radio display.

# How to reproduce

1. connect `rigctl` to TS-950SDX by `rigctl --model=2013 --rig-file=/dev/ttyUSB0 -vvvvv`
1.  send `IF` command: `W IF; 38`
    1. receive: `IF00014070030`
1. send `FA` command: `W FA; 14`
    1. receive `FA00007074000`, expect `IF00014070030`
1. send `FB` command: `W FB; 14`
    1. receive `FB00010136000`, expect `IF00014070030`

# What I tried

1. Deactivated cache; behaviour did not change:
```
   cache_timeout: "Cache timeout, value of 0 disables caching"
	Default: 500, Value: 500
   	Range: 0.0..5000.0, step 1.0
```
2. Exactly specified the connection parameters; behaviour did not change:
`rigctl --model=2013 --rig-file=/dev/ttyUSB0 --dcd-type=RIG --serial-speed=4800 --set-conf=stop_bits=2,serial_parity=None,serial_handshake=Hardware,data_bits=8 -vvvvv`
3. Configured `grig`, `flrig` or `wsjtx` or so that the frequency/band of the radio can be changed by software.
Whenever a frequency change is made by the GUI it seemingly sends a command to the radio which then beeps but the frequency on the display does not change.
4. Tried with TS-950SDX settings "Transfr" (allows data transfer between two TS-950SDX) and "Direct" (whether signals are directly written to VFO by Transfr function or not) in all variants (all off, all on, only Transfr, only Direct).

I don't know if the behaviour is caused by the radio or `hamlib` library. The RS232 connection is most likely set up correctly (baud rate, flow control, stop bits, parity, rtx/cts/rx/tx signals are inverted by the FT232RL chip, rts/cts are crossed over and so are tx/rx) because other commands work as expected: PTT, A=B, A<=>B, s-meter readout, ...

Does `kenwood_transaction: Unknown command or rig busy 'PS'` relate to the described problem?

title: String data type in XML-RPC incorrectly defined in Hamlib 4.5
body:
Hamlib 4.5 does not recognize string data type returned via XML-RPC. The reason is that this line in `rigs/dummy/flrig.c`:

`if (streq(p, "i4") || streq(p, "double") || streq(p, "int") || streq(p, " string"))`

has an extraneous space in `" string"`. It should be:

`if (streq(p, "i4") || streq(p, "double") || streq(p, "int") || streq(p, "string"))`

Thanks.

Steve AG7GN

title: Broken pkg-config test in hamlib-4.5.tar.gz

labels.name: Needs test
labels.description: Patches have been submitted but need testing to close issue

body:
Something to bear in mind for the next release...

The `hamlib-4.5.tar.gz` tarball was built on a system that didn't have `pkg.m4` available. Because of [how the pkg-config test is written](https://github.com/Hamlib/Hamlib/blob/master/configure.ac#L459) in `configure.ac`, this means that the shipped `configure` script will never detect `pkg-config`, so it's not possible to enable XML support. (It works fine if you re-bootstrap before configuring.)

It might be better to remove the fallback code, or explicitly check that XML support works in release tarballs?

title: TX-500 with Digirig not working

labels.name: Need more info
labels.description: Developer request for debugging info, etc.

body:
Hi there,

I'm trying to make rigctld run after an update of my entire OS, along with the ham-related programs.  Libhamlib, in particular, was working fine (version 4.0-7 in Devuan), but broke on this update (to 4.5-2+b1).

In order to make things easier, I just built the code I checked out from github.  Here is the output of the command using the Kenwood TS-2000 protocol (which used to work in version 4.0-7), `rigctld -m 2014 -r /dev/ttyUSB0 -vvv`:

[2014.txt](https://github.com/Hamlib/Hamlib/files/10226465/2014.txt)

Using the native TX-500 code now in hamlib, `rigctld -m 2050 -r /dev/ttyUSB0 -vvv`, I get this output:

[2050.txt](https://github.com/Hamlib/Hamlib/files/10226491/2050.txt)

While rigctld was running, I also briefly started `pat http` so something tries to use the CAT interface, but the behaviour is essentially the same with other clients (`wsjtx` etc.).  My hardware also hasn't changed, it's a TX-500 with a Digirig interface to the PC.

The Digirig connects for CAT via /dev/ttyUSB0, which is present, regardless of what the logs say.

What am I doing wrong?

title: Add Apex rotator control
body:
Baud 57,600 8,N,1

Don't know what these commands do but it was sending these continuously
[R21T11H00000000]
[R22T11H00000000]
[R23T11H00000000]
[R24T11H00000000]

Controller was sending 99 but Apex intiially was asking for 98 -- so the software needs to look at what the controller # is before sending commands.

Controller spits out one of these very 2 seconds.
This is unidirectional mode and what PSTRotator should want -- unless there's some ability for PSTRotator to understand bidirectional.
[T4BRFA99H00M0107] -- 0 degrees
[T4BRFA99H00M0100] -- 45 degrees
[T4BRFA99H00M0101] -- 90 degrees
[T4BRFA99H00M0102] -- 135 degrees
[T4BRFA99H00M0103] -- 180 degrees
[T4BRFA99H00M0104] -- 225 degrees
[T4BRFA99H00M0105] -- 270 degrees
[T4BRFA99H00M0106] -- 315 degrees


These are the bidirectional answers
[T4BRFA99H00M0200] -- 45
[T4BRFA99H00M0201] -- 90
[T4BRFA99H00M0202] -- 135
[T4BRFA99H00M0203] -- 180 Bidirectional N/S
[T4BRFA99H00M0204] -- 225
[T4BRFA99H00M0205] -- 270
[T4BRFA99H00M0206] -- 315
[T4BRFA99H00M0207] -- 0



All commands need CR added
The 98 should be replaced by whatever the rig returns -- in this case it was 99.
Startup: [LINK] returns [LINKOK]
LEFT:[R98T4AH01]  [R99T4AH01] counter 
RIGHT:[R98T4AH02] 
UNI:[R98T4AH03] [R99T4AH03]

title: FTDX5000 stuck on data port
body:
Well I just discovered a more serious issue. As you may or may not be aware, the FT5000 has the option to use the rear data jack for input and/or the front microphone jack. Via the menu I have the had the Mic Select option set to Data which allows audio input to the rear data jack while muting the front mic jack while running data which is ideal for FT8 operation. What is happening is the front mic jack is becoming totally disabled once I run the program and exit. In order for me to be able to use the front mic jack again I need to change the menu selection to Front, but then WSJT-X will not work.

If I change it back to Data and run JTDX let's say, everything again works just fine. So Something in your version of the WSJT-X is causing a serious problem. Maybe it is due to the fact that I am using Omnirig1 for the CAT and hot the FT5000.
K2QB

title: FTDX5000 EX103 behavior
QRP-Labs QDX IF command parsing buggy

labels.name: Needs test
labels.description: Patches have been submitted but need testing to close issue

body:
I'm using a QRP-Labs QDX which emulates TS-440. When requesting PTT state from rigctl (sending command 't') it returns 0 (RX) even when still transmitting.

It appears that the 440 protocol returns accurate PTT state from 'P8' of the 'IF' command as per the spec. I'm going to suggest that hamlib reads PTT state from this, rather than return 0 as it does now.

Discussion here: https://groups.io/g/QRPLabs/topic/95922381?p=Created,,,20,1,0,0::recentpostdate/sticky,,,20,2,0,95922381,previd=1672274690459582723,nextid=1672093401297648786

I might be wrong but this is as far as I've gotten in terms of debug.

title: Can't change CM108 GPIO using ptt_bitnum

labels.name: Critical
labels.description: A problem for common operations with WSJT-X, GPredict, RigPi, etc.

body:
Setting the GPIO pin for the CM108 PTT device appears to be broken.

Here's the default configuration:

```
$> rigctl -L -P CM108 | grep ptt_bitnum -A 2
rig_open: error = (null) No such file or directory 
ptt_bitnum: "Push-To-Talk GPIO bit number"
	Default: 2, Value: 0
	Range: 0.0..7.0, step 1.0
```

Setting `ptt_bitnum` shows the configuration option being set:

```
$> rigctl -L -P CM108 -C ptt_bitnum=3 | grep ptt_bitnum -A 2
rig_open: error = (null) No such file or directory 
ptt_bitnum: "Push-To-Talk GPIO bit number"
	Default: 2, Value: 3
	Range: 0.0..7.0, step 1.0
```

But when the rig is initialized, the default value is used instead of the configured value:

```
$> rigctl -L -P CM108 -p /dev/hidraw0 -C ptt_bitnum=3 -vvvv 2>&1 | grep cm108_ptt_set
cm108_ptt_set called
cm108_ptt_set: bit number 2 to state 0
^C
```

title: KX2 power calculation fails
Building hamlib while hamlib is installed fails the build
body:
I have the OS's hamlib package installed but I tried to build the latest git code to try out a recent bugfix.  The hamlib build tried to use rig.h and libhamlib.so.4 from the system directories instead of forcing the use of the ones in the source tree.  Needless to say, the mismatch caused various unexpected failures.

I saw this happen on FreeBSD, but I don't see any reason it shouldn't fail on other OSes as well.

Probably the easiest way to reproduce it reliably is to install the OS's package and hand-edit the installed rig.h to contain something like:
```
#error "should not be used"
```

Building hamlib from source should not pick up the system rig.h and therefore shouldn't error out.

Ultimately, it is an include directory ordering issue.  `-I../include` should be ahead of any `-I` directives for installed header dirs.  (On FreeBSD, external software ends up in /usr/local which may be why autotools inserts `-I/usr/local/include` into CPPFLAGS.)

title: Linux set_powerstat 0 fails to reopen

labels.name: Needs test
labels.description: Patches have been submitted but need testing to close issue

body:
When power is commanded OFF with set_powerstat 0 nothing special happens.
But when power is again commanded ON with set_powerstat 1 something weird happens.

Effect is same if USB plug is plugged to PC.
I assume IC7300 powers it USB circuits via USB cable from PC when powered OFF. That way it manages to keep the ci-v system alive waiting for possible set_power_on command.
When it finally arrives powering of USB circuit is moved from PC via USB cable to rig's own power.
(Or then just internal reset is done always for USB circuits when powered ON)
That causes small glitch that resets USB serial port and PC detects it like new USB device has been connected:

title: Would like #defines with exact hamlib version number
body:
I'm trying to support more than just the latest version of hamlib which requires knowing which bugs are present in the used version and need workarounds.  A common way of doing this is to compare the library-provide version number against a list of workarounds.

Something like this should do:

```
#define HAMLIB_VERSION_MAJOR 4
#define HAMLIB_VERSION_MINOR 5
#define HAMLIB_VERSION_PATCH 4
```

Maybe I missed it, but I didn't see anything like that in rig.h.  Could you add these or something like them to allow for easy integer comparisons?

With these, I can then conditionally disable some functionality.  E.g., KX2 power calculation doesn't work prior to 4.5.5 (I'm assuming the next version will be 4.5.5) or netrigctl prior to 4.3.1 may segfault in power2mW.

I realize that it won't help with already released versions, but it'd help with usage of future hamlib versions.

Note that hamlib_version contains "Hamlib 4.4" and therefore doesn't have enough granularity. (Also, parsing such a string in C is a headache compared to something like the #defines above.)

Thanks for taking a look.

When rigctld is started or when entering the "f" command in rigctl, rigctld sends fe fe 8c 03 fd to the ID-5100 which seems to be correct.  The ID-5100 replies with fe fe e0 8c 03 98 45 01 fd. title: WSJT-X crashes when QRG was changed on IC-9700
body:
Need to change async_data_enabled to default to on in order to handle rigs with transceive enabled properly.
Some amplifiers use transceive mode on the rigs so having this enabled by default now should be the best solution.  Probably won't be anybody that wants to turn it off.  This also helps with gpredict when twiddling the VFO knob.

title: Rig type for QRP Labs QCX series
body:
I'm currently preparing a patch for hamlib for the QRP Labs QCX series

These use the Kenwood TS480 protocol and it is by an large compatible.

However sending morse leaves long pauses between each sent item because of this code

https://github.com/Hamlib/Hamlib/blob/36c777e8bbd61600b89253656d1c6263206310cd/rigs/kenwood/kenwood.c#L4968-L4975

What I want is hamlib to treat the QCX like an Elecraft rig for the purposes of sending morse. The QCX doesn't work as an Elecraft rig though - it fails to initialise - for reasons I haven't worked out yet.

https://github.com/Hamlib/Hamlib/blob/36c777e8bbd61600b89253656d1c6263206310cd/rigs/kenwood/kenwood.c#L4961-L4966

I've made a patch adding a QCX rig type, mainly just to fix this one issue, but maybe there is a better way?

Here is a preview https://github.com/ncw/Hamlib/commit/fa277d37e0cb5d275840cd3ca1a88ca4c3c9e7e0

title: Hamlib/WSJT-X issue with SDRPlusPlus
body:
Run into a compatibility issue between [SDRPlusPlus](https://github.com/AlexandreRouma/SDRPlusPlus)  and WSJT-x (Hamlib). I detailed my findings in https://github.com/AlexandreRouma/SDRPlusPlus/issues/573, but, in short, it appears that according to the manual netrigctl should only send the VFO string if vfo_mode is set, not when vfo_option OR vfo_mode is.

Code snippet from https://github.com/Hamlib/Hamlib/blob/master/rigs/dummy/netrigctl.c#L121
`  
    if (rig->state.vfo_opt || priv->rigctld_vfo_mode)
    {
`

The consequence of the current implementation is that a server responding to the `chk_fvo` command with `CHKVFO 0` still receives the vfo string. If this is somehow expected, then I would imagine there should be a recommended response the software implementer can use to indicate the server doesn't support that option .

This may also be the root cause for https://github.com/Hamlib/Hamlib/issues/930

Hamlib version is 4.5.5 built from release tarball. Running on Fedora 38.

title: FT-8x7: Cannot switch between PKTUSB and PKTLSB
body:
I recently made some updates to the FreeDV application to support rig control. As part of this, FreeDV calls `rig_set_mode` to ensure that the application is following the agreed-upon standard for FreeDV (`RIG_MODE_PKTLSB` or `RIG_MODE_LSB` for 40 meters and below and the USB equivalents for 20 and above). During testing with my FT-817 I noticed that hamlib was not switching between `RIG_MODE_PKTLSB` and `RIG_MODE_PKTUSB`. Here's an example of what happens on 4.5.4 when I use rigctl:

```
Mooneers-16-MacBook-Pro-2461:build_osx mooneer$ rigctl -V
rigctl Hamlib 4.5.4 Jan 10 01:31:41Z 2023 SHA=921cc5
```

title: GPIO not unbound after closing.
body:
Hi,I'm using GPIO to control PTT. I have found that the gpio port is not released when rigclt/rigctld is closed. I'm using a sbc Nextthingco C.H.I.P., with the following configuration:
Linux chip 4.4.13-ntc-mlc #1 SMP Tue Dec 6 21:38:00 UTC 2016 armv7l GNU/Linux
Debian 8 (jessie), variant "Debian no C.H.I.P."
gcc (Debian 4.9.2-10+deb8u2) 4.9.2

To control my Icom IC706 I use:
#rigctl -m 3009 -c 0x48 -r /dev/ttyS0 -s 19200 -P GPIO -p 1013
where 1013 is the gpio port number.
It works perfectly the first time, but if I close rigctl and open it again, it won't communicate with the rig. The solution is to unbind the port with: 
#sh -c 'echo 1013 > /sys/class/gpio/unexport'
I suggest this should be included in the gpio_close function. 
I'm not a real developer, so it will take long until I fix it in the code. If I get it done I will submit the solution to github. 
Thanks for the hard work.

labels.description: Patches have been submitted but need testing to close issue

body:
When specifying flrig as the rig in WSJT-X, the rig mode is not set to
"DATA/USB" even if "Data/Pkt" is specified as the mode.
The "WSJT-X_RigControl.log" shows the following messages:
[RIGCTRL:error] modeMapGetFLRig: FlRig does not have mode: PKTUSB

I currently work around this by manually setting it to "DATA/USB".
If possible, set "DATA/USB" when "Data/Pkt".
Rig is FTdx3000DM
No problem if it is "USB" instead of "Data/Pkt"

title: Elecraft K4 PSK mode not switching to data when changed
body:
I was watching W1AW on PSK (20M) when I opted to go to FT8.

The WSJT-X (2.5.4) program is connected by itself to one of the K4
ports.  It wouldn't shift to data mode.  Any other mode, except PSK,
would change to data mode with WSJT-X (on band select).  I was able to
telnet the DT0; to change modes, so it's not a K4 flaw.

This appears to be a flaw in WSJT-X 2.5.4.  It is not band dependent, if
in PSK on any band, changing to data isn't happening without a user
screen tap or telnet command.  The control command must include DT0; to
allow FT8 to work, if coming from PSK mode (probably a safe default
anyway).

It's not a huge deal, I'm just passing it along in case someone knows
where to have an adjustment made in WSJT-X.

73,
Rick NK7I

title: IC-7300 stops tracking the frequency after some time
body:
I see the following behaviour on the IC-7300 with version 4.6-git (aa1cf567): after some time I cannot get the current frequency using get_freq anymore. Instead I get the value that is in the cache. The cached value is not updated, so I keep getting the same value, no matter what frequency is selected on the radio.

I tried to disable the cache using `-C cache_timeout=0`, but in the trace I see that `use_cached_freq` changes from 0 to 1 at some point.

I found no way to reproduce the problem immediately, but I found out that changing the band or doing fast frequency changes makes the problem occur sooner.

This issue may be related to #1108.

[dump_frequency_tracking.txt](https://github.com/Hamlib/Hamlib/files/10449683/dump_frequency_tracking.txt)

title: FTDX3000 reverse split support
body:
FTDX3000 reverse split support needs to be investigate (and other Yaesu models)
WSJTX does not turn split on during startup but does recognize when rig is already in split mode.
When reverse split (VFOB=Rx, VFOA=Tx) occurs the wrong FT3 command is being sent.  Could have to do with Main/Sub VFO names.
FT2 should be sent instead of FT3 when VFOB=Rx.

title: Rig port_type in case of SERIAL/NETWORK Rig
body:
Is there any way  how to distinguish whether a given rig is `SERIAL`-only, `NETWORK`-Only or `SERIAL/NETWORK` ? 

An example is this

```
    .model_name = "PiHPSDR",
    .mfg_name =  "OpenHPSDR",
    .version =  BACKEND_VER ".1",
    .copyright =  "LGPL",
    .status =  RIG_STATUS_STABLE,
    .rig_type =  RIG_TYPE_TRANSCEIVER,
    .ptt_type =  RIG_PTT_RIG,
    .dcd_type =  RIG_DCD_RIG,
    .port_type =  RIG_PORT_SERIAL,
```
The rig can be connected via `SERIAL` port and `NETWORK` but .port_type  can contain only one type - in this case SERIAL port.

title: Extended Response Protocol not consistent with u command
body:
If I use the Extended Response Protocol (ERP) by adding a comma to the start of a line, some commands return RPRT at the end of the one line separated by the comma, but other commands send the RPRT 0 on a newline. This is inconsistent with the documentation and makes it hard to use the ERP.



``` dos
C:\Windows\system32>echo ,v | ncat -w 1 localhost 4532
get_vfo: currVFO,VFO: VFOA,RPRT 0

C:\Windows\system32>echo ,f VFOA | ncat -w 1 localhost 4532
get_freq: VFOA,Frequency: 14161050,RPRT 0

C:\Windows\system32>echo ,u VFOA RIT | ncat -w 1 localhost 4532
get_func: VFOA RIT,1
RPRT 0

```

Note this appears to be multiple get_func (u) command as I tried RIT XIT and NR.

title: send_voice_mem for K4 and K3

labels.name: Needs test
labels.description: Patches have been submitted but need testing to close issue

body:
The command to play a voice memory on the K4 is to send the following:

``` pascal
Self.SendToRadio(Format('DAMP%d00000;',[mem]));  // DAMPmnnnnn; where mem is mem number and nnnnn is repeat in ms (set to 00000)
```

The radio supports 8 memories.

The command to stop playing the voice is Self.SendToRadio('DA0;');  // DA0; Stops all DVK activity

It does not appear there is a stop_voice like there is for stop_morse so I presume we can just set the rig to Receive?

The command to send the K3 memories are as follows (only 4 memories on the K3):

``` delphi
case mem of
   1: localMsg := 'SWT21;';
   2: localMsg := 'SWT31;';
   3: localMsg := 'SWT35;';
   4: localMsg := 'SWT39;';
end
```
The command to stop voice playback on the K3 is 'SWT37;'

title: Kenwood voice stop not working
body:
OK The play works… but I think the Stop is problematic.

 

Currently the voice command for the Icom/Yaesu and TS590 is a single character for channel number, where 1 is the first channel and 0 channel is stop message.

 

The TS890 has two bytes for channel number and operation.

 

Here is the stop cmd you send.

 

15:14:50.723 Send Voice Memory Number 0 to rig

15:14:50.723 Hamlib:  2:rig.c(7105):rig_send_voice_mem entered

15:14:50.723 Hamlib:  3:kenwood.c(5347):kenwood_send_voice_mem entered

15:14:50.723 Hamlib:  kenwood_transaction called cmd=PB101

15:14:50.723 Hamlib:  kenwood_transaction: cmdstr = PB101

15:14:50.723 Hamlib:  write_block(): TX 6 bytes, method=2

15:14:50.723 Hamlib:  0000    50 42 31 30 31 3b                                   PB101;

 

Here you are sending 0 for channel number (stop for other radios) and 1 for operation, which is play on the 890. 0 is not a valid channel number on the 890….

 

To stop channel 1, the message would be PB110; Start channel 2, PB121; then stop channel 2 PB120;

 

I wonder if the 890S allows multiple messages to play at once. Anyway, I presume Hamlib doesn’t want to keep track of the channel number? So does that mean the api needs two parameters, or another function setVoiceChannelNumber(int chanNum)?

 

73 de David M0DGB/G8FKH

title: Question: Setting frequency of another VFO when split is not enabled
body:
Mainly a question to @mdblack98:

The way \set_split_freq works now is that it sets the frequency of the TX VFO. In case split is enabled (for the opposite for, e.g. for VFOB when RX is at VFOA), this works correctly and as expected.

However, when split is NOT enabled, the TX VFO is the same as RX VFO, so \set_split_freq changes the RX VFO freq -- effect is the same as with \set_freq.

My question: Is there any mechanism currently to set the frequency/mode of another VFO when split is NOT enabled? Many rigs support this, as you know.

title: ID-5100 Dual Watch mode
body:
Concerning gpredict...  I see that when gpredict is setup for Duplex TRX, Read PTT and Main ^ / Sub v, then gpredict sends a S command to rigctrld to set the Main VFO for TX.  Then it uses the I and i commands for setting and getting the TX frequency.  It uses the F and f commands for setting and getting the RX frequency.  It also uses the t command to get the PTT status.

What do you think about getting Hamlib, in the case of the ID-5100, to:

  * Assume the A band (left side of the rig) is the uplink (Main) and the B band (right side of the rig) is the downlink (Sub);

  * Upon receiving the S command, set the rig's VFO mode (cmd 07) so that the A band is the Main.
  * When an I or i command is received, and if PTT is not active, change the rig's VFO mode so that A band is Main (In case the user changed it on the rig's panel), set or get the frequency.

  * When a F or f command is received, and if PTT is not active, change the rig's VFO mode so that B band is Main, set or get the frequency, and change the rig's VFO mode so that A band is Main.
The prerequisites would be:

  * The rig is in Dualwatch mode with Main on the left side.

  * Both sides (A and B bands) must be set to VFO mode (not memory mode).

  * The ID5100 rig interface in gpredict must be set to Duplex TRX, Read PTT and Main ^/Sub v.

title: Add RIG_LEVEL_USB_AF
body:
Many rigs (e.g. IC7300) have the ability to set the USB AF level controlling audio over the USB cable to the rig.
This usually includes the ACC jack.
Adding this will allow WSJTX and JTDX and others to create their own AGC control by adjusting the USB AF level first and then the RF gain as a backup to reduce audio.
Ideally for FT8 modes and such the RF gain should be maxed out, computer audio at 0dB, and adjust the USB AF level to get the proper audio level of 70dB in WJSTX and 82dB in JTDX (RMS and Peak meter respectively) as a minimum value.

Rigs added so far
IC-705
IC-7300
IC_7610
IC-9700
IC-785X
IC-R8600

title: Killing rigctld on Windows leaves protocol in funky state
body:
**Background**
I'm creating a GoLang VARA [launcher](https://github.com/islandmagic/varanny) utility that triggers rigctld as needed. Because Windows lacks a graceful process shutdown mechanism, rigctld gets force closed when the session ends.

**Issue**
The problem sequence is:

1. Rigctld launches and functions normally at first.
2. The launcher force closes rigctld when the session is over.
3. Upon the second launch, rigctld usually encounters errors.

Rigctld is invoked with this command:
`C:\Program Files\hamlib-w64-4.5.5\bin\rigctld.exe -m 3085 -c 0xA4 -r COM7 -s 9600 -vvv`

The forced shutdown seems to leave the COM port or rig in a peculiar state. After a while, it appears to reset itself, but most commands return `RPRT -8` or `RPRT -9` codes in the meantime.

**Questions**

1. Can rigctld be shut down from the connection? Currently, I use a q command, but that only disconnects.
2. Is there a way to reset rigctld at startup to ensure it functions correctly?
3. Other suggestions?

title: include/hamlib/config.h in the tarball breaks readline support

labels.name: Needs test
labels.description: Patches have been submitted but need testing to close issue

labels.name: Priority
labels.description: High priority for enhancement or fix but not critical

body:
Hi,

#947 shuffled the config.h header around so "HAVE_PTHREAD is available if needed".

This causes a chain of events:
* hamlib/config.h was added to nobase_include_HEADERS in include/Makefile.am
* the `make dist` tarball now contains a static `include/hamlib/config.h`
* when doing an out-of-tree (VPATH) build, `build/include/hamlib.config.h` is generated
* the `-I` flags on the compiler command line list the top source include directory before any out-of-tree build directory
* since the tarball config.h is preferred over the config.h generated by ./configure, none of the non-default flags in there is visible to .c files
* `test/.libs/rigctl` and `test/.libs/rotctl` aren't using libreadline anymore (note that the compiler command line still has `-lreadline`, but the `#ifdef` in the file doesn't trigger)
```
/bin/bash ../libtool  --tag=CC   --mode=link gcc -Wall  -I../src -I../security -g -O2 -ffile-prefix-map=/<<PKGBUILDDIR>>=. -fstack-protector-strong -Wformat -Werror=format-security   -Wl,-z,relro -Wl,-z,now -o rigctld rigctld-rigctld.o rigctld-rigctl_parse.o rigctld-dumpcaps.o   ../src/libhamlib.la ../lib/libmisc.la -ldl -lreadline
```
* the Debian libhamlib-utils package doesn't even depend on libreadline anymore

TBH I don't see why 9aade8de3f52 had to add config.h to nobase_include_HEADERS - the net patch there seems to be
```
-#ifdef _PTHREAD_H
+#ifdef HAVE_PTHREAD
```
and that should have worked without forcing config.h to be included in `make install` or `make dist`. Is that file of any use on end-user systems?

I think the fix is simply reverting the include/Makefile.am part:

```
diff --git a/include/Makefile.am b/include/Makefile.am
index 324c082f4..bba8cdc13 100644
--- a/include/Makefile.am
+++ b/include/Makefile.am
@@ -3,4 +3,4 @@ noinst_HEADERS = bandplan.h num_stdio.h
 nobase_include_HEADERS = hamlib/rig.h hamlib/riglist.h hamlib/rig_dll.h \
 		hamlib/rotator.h hamlib/rotlist.h hamlib/rigclass.h \
 		hamlib/rotclass.h hamlib/amplifier.h hamlib/amplist.h \
-		hamlib/ampclass.h hamlib/config.h hamlib/multicast.h
+		hamlib/ampclass.h hamlib/multicast.h
```

Does that make sense? If yes, I can throw it in as pull request.

title: Meaning of targeted VFO with \set_split_freq commands
body:
@mdblack98 Again, maybe you know this best.

I'm trying to understand the *intended* function of the targeted VFO (in VFO mode) for the `\set_split_freq` command.

I'm looking at the three major backend implementations: Yaesu (newcat), Kenwood and Icom.

# Yaesu/Kenwood split freq set

With the Yaesu and Kenwood implementations, the `\set_split_freq` isn't usually even implemented, as it's delegated back to `\set_freq`, because Yaesu/Kenwood have the `FA`/`FB` commands to target both VFOs.

It looks like Yeasu/Kenwood use the VFO argument, depending on split (via vfo_fixup) with this fallback when `\set_split_freq` is not implemented:

* https://github.com/Hamlib/Hamlib/blob/680ce55ba26df1e3634356229bfe20491706f77e/src/rig.c#L4314

So using `\set_split_vfo VFOB 14215000` would indeed target VFOB (when split is not enabled), but it would result in VFOA change when split is already enabled.

-> Question 1: Is this the intended behavior? Sounds a bit confusing that a targeted VFO (if it is not a relative one, such as VFO_CURR, VFO_TX or VFO_OTHER) would still get translated to an opposite VFO *depending on split state*! I completely understand that the behavior *should be like that* for VFO_CURR, VFO_TX and VFO_OTHER -- but maybe not for the "absolute" VFOs, such as VFOA?

Anyway, with Yaesu/Kenwood the logic is rather simple and predictable (regardless of the confusing split behavior).

# Icom split freq set

With Icom, the `\set_split_freq` looks even more complicated (and yes, I know it needs to be, as there is no way to get the current VFO -- though newer rigs with Main/Sub support targeting via the 0x25 command).

Icom logic doesn't even check the VFO parameter here:

* https://github.com/Hamlib/Hamlib/blob/680ce55ba26df1e3634356229bfe20491706f77e/rigs/icom/icom.c#L5618
* https://github.com/Hamlib/Hamlib/blob/680ce55ba26df1e3634356229bfe20491706f77e/rigs/icom/icom.c#L5839

And even in those cases (get/set) the logic is slightly different...?

-> Question 2: Is the Icom logic maybe just a "remnant" from a series of changes over the years? To me it looks like it doesn't address all the scenarios properly and doesn't provide consistent behavior.

What I'd like to do is just to make the Icom set_split_freq (and mode) logic use the 0x25 and 0x26 commands more consistently (and with predictable logic, also in the VFO mode) AND -- most importantly -- correctly target the MAIN/SUB VFOs on the rigs that have them (e.g. IC-7600, IC-7610, IC-7800, IC-785x and IC-9700). The rest of the rigs (with VFOA/VFOB and the selected/unselected VFO-based 0x25/0x26 commands) need to be a bit inaccurate, just like now.

I've got an IC-7300, an IC-9700, an IC-7600 and an IC-7610 all available for testing my changes. I'd just first like to confirm what the intended behavior would be and if I should follow the Kenwood/Yaesu example or even change that one too (regarding the targeted VFO mode).

title: Change token_t to hamlib_token_t to avoid collision with libbsm
body:
/*

 * Contents of token_t are opaque outside of libbsm.

 */

typedef struct au_token token_t;


It is part of libbsm, a security library originally from FreeBSD. The problem on macOS is that if hamlib is used in a Xcode project, pretty much all system header files are included automatically though Cocoa.h or Framework.h.

It is present in macOS Sonoma and has been for at least the last 8-9 years, or longer.

Best Regards,
Chris

title: Error on current hamlib with Xiegu X6100 and truSDX

labels.name: Needs test
labels.description: Patches have been submitted but need testing to close issue

body:
Preparing my holiday ham radio equipment i tried to set up wsjtx 271 (dev) with my truSDX with the current firmware (2.00u and 2.00x as second try) and with my Xiegu X6100, both connected via USB. 
Connection parameters set under Win10 in device-manager from 19200 to max of 115200 or so, parameters for 8,N,1 unchanged to last time, it worked with the same setup, but older WSJTX-version (2.5.4, but no more installed). 

When connection truSDX with truSDX driver-programm every time WSJTX mentions hamlib errors, that connection to the rig is absolutely impossible due to connection timeouts. So enough time wasted with truSDX i tried my Xiegu and also errors occur, which i added as attachement. The main statement is "Feature not available". 
![hamliberror_x6100](https://github.com/Hamlib/Hamlib/assets/149412955/a6927a4a-55a1-41dc-85cf-1d975946aaab)

Trying different settings (as other baud rate) the connection is either "rejected" or "timed out" or "protocol error", especially when changing on the other com port or - new error - getting "feature not available while getting current mode". 

I tried with the current firmware of my xiegu on 4 (!) different windows 10-laptops and desktops and got the same results. 

So where's my fault? What's wrong with the setup? What's eventually wrong with hamlib 4.6 from 2024-01-30? 

HELP... 
Thanks and cheers, 73 Cornel DK5CR

[ADDED:] Just tried to us Xiegu X108G as device and few seconds later "Test CAT"-Button jumped to green with the same settings but the rig. Also PTT worked. BUT: Audio line via USB crashes, cause X6100 loses its audio devices, perhaps due to some CAT-commands. Also works on X5105 with CAT, but PTT doesn't work properly (letting lose PTT occurs an error). 

So it seems to be a specific error-issue for the X6100 in the hamlib library.

title: Xiegu X6100 responds with frequency multiplied by 100
body:
Reproduction steps:

1. Downloaded the windows binaries from https://n0nb.users.sourceforge.net/ (https://n0nb.users.sourceforge.net/hamlib-w64-4.6~git-20240320-538d41b9e.zip)

2. Tune radio to 14.074.000

3. Query the frequency with rigctl:

    ```
    bin\rigctl.exe -m 3087 -r COM3 f
    1407400000
    ```
    
    It's giving 2 extra zeros:
    
    14074000**00**

4. Setting the frequency works correctly using the correct value of 14074000:

    ```
    bin\rigctl.exe -m 3087 -r COM3 F 14074000
    ```

I think this is making WSJT-X report back the frequency incorrectly, even though setting it works:

![image](https://github.com/Hamlib/Hamlib/assets/1486609/0dee3a34-6c3b-489d-acbb-0e92791ba372)
https://github.com/Hamlib/Hamlib/issues/1499#issuecomment-2004551779


X6100 Firmware is V1.1.7

title: Rigctl timeout when sending raw (extended) command that gets a response.

labels.name: Needs test
labels.description: Patches have been submitted but need testing to close issue

body:
Struggling with the use of some extended commands of an Anan G2 SDR.
Using the rigctl basic command set and model Kenwood TS2000 (which the Anan emulates), e.g. to ask for the transmit frequency, works fine.
But querying the Anan with an extended command, using the w option (send command), the command times out even though the Anan answers correctly.
Problem is that the routine in rigctl that does the communication is not given the proper expected length of an answer (it doesn't know the command) and once past the default 1 length value it misses the ';' that ends the answer that was given and keeps waiting for more, that does not come, until time out.
It has worked correctly in the past. Problem exists in current Hamlib.

title: Generic RTS PTT device
body:
Background: Linux users trying to use a Baofeng using a Digirig using software that depends on Hamlib

Firstly, I am aware of rigctl's invocation for what I am asking for: `rigctld --ptt-file=/dev/ttyUSB0 --ptt-type=RTS`

New users may have an issue with there not being a rigfile, as when/how do do a generic serial RTS ptt is not readily apparent (outside of writing your own software), and often not covered in any other manuals. The workflow for using rigctld is usually "find your rig" -> "set your rig and serial port."

It would make it much easier for users of generic RTS PTT devices (such as the Digirig: digirig.net) to have a rigfile that does the same thing as above. It would eliminate a lot of confusion and be much like the normal 'hamlib workflow'.

`rigctld -l` may show
```
 Rig #   Mfg                    Model                   Version         Status      Macro
12345    Digirig                Generic                 202405031.0     Stable      RIG_RTS_GENERIC

``` 

`rigctld -m 12345 -r /dev/ttyUSB0` would be equivalent to `rigctld --ptt-file=/dev/ttyUSB0 --ptt-type=RTS`

I have no experience contributing to Hamlib but if nobody experienced hops up, I'll give it a shot.

title: IC-9700 set/get Sub VFO data

labels.name: Needs test
labels.description: Patches have been submitted but need testing to close issue

labels.name: Critical
labels.description: A problem for common operations with WSJT-X, GPredict, RigPi, etc.

body:
Just compiled the latest git version of Hamlib an cannot get rigctl to read/write the frequency/mode of the sub VFO. It instead return the frequency of the main VFO. Setting the VFO to SubA switches the VFO but the returned frequency is wrong:

```
~/Hamlib$ ./tests/rigctl -m 3081 -r /dev/ic-9700a -s 57600 

Rig command: V SubA

Rig command: f
Frequency: 144040010

Rig command: V MainA

Rig command: f
Frequency: 144040010
```

![20231220_214548](https://github.com/Hamlib/Hamlib/assets/7112907/fddd026e-6972-44e6-bd1c-becf60989f63)

title: Flex Slice remote operation not working

labels.name: Critical
labels.description: A problem for common operations with WSJT-X, GPredict, RigPi, etc.

body:
1. If the Flex is in the same LAN as the notebooks/pc's everything works fine and all the issues discussed before are gone (exactly the same findings as Joe had before already).

2. I could not confirm Mike's statement  "...but WSJT-X will not follow the rig yet". If I change a frequency in the flex on notebook 1 WSJT on notebook 2 is following the radio frequency setting. 

3. If the Flex is operated as remote radio in a separate LAN I was unable to get CAT to work. When I open SmartSDR locally and if I then enter the network address  provided by the Flex set up information as address in Network Server in the WSJT-settings then an error message will occur (unable to connect to xxx: 4992). I believe, however, it was not the intention of the new hamlib to provide a solution for the radio operated at a remote site. If you would still like to offer a solution for those conditions as well then I will start to do all the recording and send the files to you.

Anyway: I am already very glad for the solution for the same LAN. Thank you very much for the efforts you have spent so far!

73

Juergen, DL8LE

title: Request : integrate my hamlib REST API
body:
Hi folks,

I've started writing a REST API to network-enable hamlib, at least as far as rigctl and rotctl are concerned.

You can easily access a method of it by invoking an HTTP request against i.e.

http://192.168.12.10/trx/0/frequency ,

which will internally be translated to "rigctl -m {model} -p {interface} {interface parameters} f", for example. 

Of course, you can also set values as per

curl -XPOST 192.168.12.10/rigctl_api/trx/0/mode -d'{"mode":"FM","passband":9000}'

In a very early alpha, I've already implemented most functionality of these two tools, and it's already capcable of using more than one TRX / rotator.

Have a look at it at [](https://github.com/DL4OCE/hamlib_api_dl4oce) . All it takes for a test-drive is a VM or somethin as tiny as a Raspberry Pi Zero 2W.

My goal would be to enable users to use their rotators by simply supplying the rotator and the attached RasPi with power and connect it to the LAN by WiFi to avoid putting high voltage lines over the yard as well as building browser-based TRX GUIs, for example. Probably it will also be easy to convince logbook software creators to support the new, easy interface, in their programs? And son on...

Let me know if you've got any questions about this and if you're interested in integrating this with the hamlib bundle, or if I should keep it separate...

Vy 73 de Arne, DL4OCE ..._._

title: IC-9700 reports incorrect power
body:
The ICOM IC-9700 has 3 bands.  Each band has a different maximum power:
* 2m has a max of 100W
* 70cm has a max of 75W
* 23cm has a max of 10W

hamlib misreports the currently selected power because it doesn't seem to scale the percentage of max power by the max power for that band.  For example, if one selects 60% on 23cm, hamlib will report 60W instead of 6W.

Looking at hamlib's code, it looks like `icom_power2mW` special cases IC-705 and IC-905 (making the assumption that 10W is the max on all bands; I don't know if that's correct), but assumes that all other models are 100W max on all bands. The `icom_mW2power` function just assumes 100W max regardless of model or band.

title: FT-817nd Problem, Commit 32e6b90
body:
Commit 32e6b90

Lines 189 and 190 should not have been changed this way...
189 - { 1, { 0x0a, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x07 } }, /* mode set main DIG /
190 - { 1, { 0x0c, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x07 } }, / mode set main PKT /
189 + { 1, { 0x0a, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x0a } }, / mode set main DIG /
190 + { 1, { 0x0c, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x0c } }, / mode set main PKT */

The original 189 & 190 were correct for the FT-817. Please revert.

An update... After a half-day trying to figure out why my radio CAT control would not work properly, even with older commits of Hamlib, I determined that this change, and possibly others(?) since this commit corrupted the memory in my radio and it would incorrectly respond to CAT frequency and other commands. Restoring my FT-817nd from a backup using Chirp fixed the problem. So, something here is somewhat "dangerous" to the radio firmware. It might be best to avoid writing to FT-817 firmware, and just use only the officially-published CAT commands. READING from firmware is not dangerous, so that part would be fine. The NVRAM chip in the FT-817 series of radios has very limited specifications on WRITE cycles, so that is best to avoid.

73,
-Joe-
K0OG

title: Icom IC-707 CI-V Scan Bug:  Cannot scan VFO

labels.name: Needs test
labels.description: Patches have been submitted but need testing to close issue

body:
Version:  rigctld Hamlib 4.6~git 2024-09-29
OS:  Windows 10 x64
Radio:  Icom IC-707 via XGGComms USB-Digimode-4 on COM4

### Very brief tl;dr:
On the Icom IC-707, Hamlib cannot start a scan in VFOA/VFOB.  It will scan in MEM VFO, but not in VFOA/VFOB.  Using raw CI-V command does scan in VFO as expected, but not Hamlib.

Two small notes:  It seems "g ?" should return "STOP" as a supported function;  the code that emits "icom_scan: unsupported scan 0x20" is missing a newline, which makes the debug output confusing.

### Details:
I'm working my way through the IC-707 manual and the CI-V reference manual (3rd edition) and comparing them to the results from Hamlib.  I've gotten to Scan functions.

The IC-707 manual describes scans in both VFO mode (from VFOA or VFOB), and in MEM mode (from MEM VFO).  The CI-V reference manual describes only one command 0x0e with only two subcommands:  0x00 to stop a scan, and 0x01 to start a scan.

Using the CI-V commands manually seems to work as the IC-707 manual describes.  When the radio is in one of the actual VFO's (VFOA/VFOB), sending "... 0x0e 0x01 ..." starts the scan:  "SCAN" appears on the radio display and the current frequency begins to increase.  When the radio is in the MEM VFO, sending the same command starts the scan as well:  "SCAN" appears on the radio display and the current memory channel begins to increase.  In either case, sending "... 0x0e 0x00 ..." stops the scan:  "SCAN" disappears on the radio display and the frequency or memory channel stops increasing.  This behavior matches what the radio manual describes.

Howver, this does not work with Hamlib.  First, there seems to be a bit of a disconnect between the CI-V interface and the Hamlib interface.  Hamlib seems to have a single command:  "g".  This command takes two parameters:  "Scan Fct" (I assume function), and "Scan Channel".  A "g ?" gives me the string "VFO MEM", so it seems there are two functions for my radio:  VFO and MEM.  This seems to agree with the radio manual.  I don't really have a "Scan Channel".  It seems that while the number is required (the parser won't continue without it), it doesn't matter what number I use for this radio.  I've been using "0" because it seems to cause the least issues for me.

So, now to use the functions.  Starting with MEM, the results seem to work in a reasonable way.  If I give Hamlib a "g MEM 0", the radio will put itself into the MEM VFO (no matter what VFO I started from), and then begin the scan.  If I then use the "STOP" Scan Fct (i.e. "g STOP 0"), the scan stops.  (An aside:  It would be useful if a "g ?" reported "STOP" as well as VFO and MEM...  It *is* a valid function!)  So far, so good.

However, I do not have the same results with the VFO Scan Fct.  If I give Hamlib a "g VFO 0", I get a "RPRT -1" and nothing happens.  It does not matter what VFO I am in or any other changes I make, I always get that same error.  This is a different error than if I were to alter the ScanFct.  For example, if I give Hamlib a "g VFOA 0", I get a "RPRT -11".  So Hamlib is definitely trying to do something with my "g VFO 0" command, but something is wrong.

I increased to debug output and re-tried the commands.  I've included the output below.  First is the output from executing a "g MEM 0", waiting a few seconds and then executing a "g STOP 0".  These work successfully.  The second output is from executing a "g VFO 0".

The relevant part of the failed output seems to be this:  "icom_scan: unsupported scan 0x20".  (NOTE:  there seems to be an error in the code that generated the output of that line:  it's missing a newline.  You will see what I'm talking about if you look at the failed logs below.  It made it a bit difficult to figure out what the actual error ouptput was.)

An examination of the CI-V documentation I have (including radios up to the early 2000's) does *not* have either an 0x20 command nor a 0x20 subcommand for the 0x0e command.  So I'm not sure what this command is for, or why Hamlib is trying this command.  Possibly something that works for modern radios?

In any case, I'm not sure where to go from here.  MEM scans work, VFO scans do not.  Both work with manual CI-V commands.  I would greatly appreciate any help you might be able to give me.

Once again, thank you very much for all of your work on Hamlib.  It's an incredible resource for those of us who love to combine computers and radios.  I'm amazed how well it works, even with a seemingly-unpopular radio from more than 30 years ago.  And I saw that my previous issue is already fixed!  I'll test that right now!  Thank you very much.

---

```
2024-10-03T18:05:37.292271-0500: mutex_rigctld: client lock engaged
```

title: Icom IC-707 CI-V Bugs:  memory clear, memory ranges and tuning steps
body:
Version:  rigctld Hamlib 4.6~git 2024-09-29
OS:  Windows 10 x64
Radio Icom IC-707 via XGGComms USB-Digimode-4 on COM4.

### Very brief tl;dr:
There seem to be a couple of mistakes in the IC-707 rig code.  This rig does **not** support memory clear (CI-V command 0x0b), and it **does** support tuning steps (CI-V command 0x10 sub 0x00 and 0x01).  Also, the memory ranges are incorrect:  it supports 1-25 single memories, 26-30 split (dual) memories and 31-32 scan edge memories.

Also, a couple of small questions:  what does "E" mean in capabilities, and it seems that `--show-conf` now exits the daemon instead of letting it run?  Finally, if there's any other testing I can do for the IC-707, please let me know.

### Details:
I just acquired a new-in-box Icom IC-707 radio -- yes, it sat on a prepper's shelf for 30 years!  I bought this radio with almost no knowledge of this radio.  I saw that it's missing a *lot* of buttons you'd normally have...  But I **did** check to see that this radio was supported by Hamlib.  It was, so I figured I was good to go:  I can use rig control to make up for the lack of buttons, right?

Now that I own it, I've now found that this is a bit of a rare model.  There is *very* little documentation for this radio outside of the basic user's manual.  Most importantly, there is no CI-V information specifically for this radio.  In addition, this is my first older radio:  I had no idea how limited early rig control was in these older devices...

The first goal was to find out what radio this was closest to.  After much frustrating testing, it seems that this radio is **very** close to the same CI-V features as an IC-737.  I was able to make all documented IC-737 CI-V commands work except the antenna select command (0x12) because the IC-707 only has a single antenna port, and some of the tuning steps (0x10):  the IC-737 supports a bunch, and the IC-707 supports less.  It's also very similar to the IC-IC-725/726/728/729, except the IC-707 does not support the memory clear command (0x0b), and adds the above-mentioned tuning step command.

However, when comparing the features I've tested to those available in Hamlib, I've found a few differences.  I thought I would document them here in the hopes that someone might be able to make the changes to correct the IC-707 model. I've cut out the relevant items from the output of --dump-caps and added notes from my testing:

```
VFO Ops: CPY FROM_VFO TO_VFO MCL
```
Does "MCL" mean Memory clear?  708 does not have memory clear from my actual testing:  CI-V 0x0b command returns ... 0xfa ... .  That seems to be verified by checking the --dump-caps from the IC-737, which does *NOT* list "MCL" as a VFO Ops.  Assming "MCL" is CI-V command 0x0b, this should be removed from the IC-707.

```
Memories:2024-10-01T10:52:55.448178-0500: rig_strmtype called

        1..26:          MEM
          Mem caps: FREQ MODE WIDTH 2024-10-01T10:52:55.448178-0500: rig_strmtype called

        27..30:         EDGE
          Mem caps: FREQ MODE WIDTH 2024-10-01T10:52:55.448178-0500: rig_strmtype called

        31..35:         SAT
          Mem caps: FREQ MODE WIDTH
```
This differs from the actual memory configuration of the IC-707:  1-25 Normal single-frequency; 26-30 Split dual-frequency; 31-32 Scan edge channels (high and low limits for VFO scan).  Page 25 of IC-707 manual (Page 28 of PDF).

```
Tuning steps:
        10.0 Hz:        AM CW USB LSB FM
Tuning steps status:    OK (0)
```
The radio physically supports three tuning steps:  10Hz, 1kHz and 1MHz.  Using CI-V command 0x10 I can only get two of them to work:  10Hz (subcommand 0x00) and 1kHz (subcommand 0x01).  I could not find a subcommand for 1MHz.  The IC-737 does not have a 1MHz tuning step option:  my guess is this was added to the IC-707 to overcome the lack of band buttons and 10-digit number pad and wasn't added to the CI-V interface.  However, if anyone has any ideas to find the 1MHz tuning step I'm happy to test!

```
Can set Tuning Step:    N
Can get Tuning Step:    N
```
See above regarding tuning steps.  (Though I **think** "get Tuning Step" is not supported.)

```
Can set Transceive:     E
Can set Channel:        E
Can get Channel:        E
```
What is "E"?  (At least it matches the IC-737...)

There's one other detail I've found updating to the lastest daily build:  Does --show-conf now exit on use?  I really liked being able to use --show-conf in my normal use just to ensure that all of my settings were correct -- I tweak things frequently and it's handy to have all of the settings listed in my logs when I start the daemon...  If that was intentional, I would suggesting updating the manpage to add that detail -- just like it does for --dump-caps.

Finally, are there any settings for the IC-707 that should be better tested?  I know that until recently the IC-707 rig was in Alpha state, and might have ony been moved to Beta because no one complained for a long time -- because maybe no one is using it?  :)  But if there's anything that I can do to further test the rig code I'm more than happy to do so!

Thank you very much for all of your hard work on Hamlib.  It has **greatly** benefitted **everyone** who connects their computer to their radio.  I hope that I can help make the IC-707 a little bit more complete and correct.

title: rig.h uses va_list without including stdarg.h
body:
Observed in 4.6.

`include/rig.h` uses `va_list` but doesn't `#include <stdarg.h>` as [POSIX requires](https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9799919799/basedefs/stdarg.h.html).   On at least NetBSD, and likely other systems, the things that POSIX requires of `stdarg.h` are not provided if it is not included.

The fix is easy if you are willing to require C99 or POSIX.

```
--- include/hamlib/rig.h.orig   2024-12-26 12:58:56.497059287 +0000
+++ include/hamlib/rig.h
@@ -36,6 +36,7 @@
 #define HAMLIB_TRACE rig_debug(RIG_DEBUG_TRACE,"%s%s(%d) trace\n",spaces(STATE(rig)->depth), __FILE__, __LINE__)
 #define __FILENAME__ (strrchr(__FILE__, '/') ? strrchr(__FILE__, '/') + 1 : __FILE__)

+#include <stdarg.h>
 #include <stdio.h>
 #include <string.h>
 #include <inttypes.h>
```

title: ICOM 7800 set Frequency command fails
body:
Environment  Linux NIXOS 24.11 (latest) 
WSJTX version 2.6.1
Hamlib (rigctl) version 4.5.5

Equipment ICOM7800 + Digi keyer II (using mhuxd to control the Digi Keyer II - a story in itself!) 

Set frequency command fails to ICOM 7800 

Test error reported by wsjtx is in the attached file hamliberror.txt
[hamliberror.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/18311536/hamliberror.txt)

I have spend a few hours trying to debug the issue and the other file I have uploaded are a read frequency and set frequency command will full verbose settings -vvvvv

[rigctltest.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/18311557/rigctltest.txt)

Line 553 > Rig command : f  
This 'works' in that it does return the frequency. However, there are many 'protocol errors' and 'Command rejected by rig' in the sequence.

Line 688 > Rig command: F 1407000

This command does not set the frequency. (Fails),  reading between the lines, it seems to lose the VCO setting (Main, Sub) and therefore fails to set the frequency ?

Current workarounds
- I will try 4.6.x of hamlib, once I figure out how to update NIXOS with the latest version.
- In WSJTX you can set the rig to be FLRig, and in FLRig (V2.0.05) use IC-7800. 
- This bypasses the use of hamlib for controlling the radio. (if FLRig is set to use hamlib then it also fails to control the radio)

b.t.w Thanks for this great program... from the little debugging  I have done.... the complexity of the keeping it working for so many radios must be crazy difficult. ! 

Martin EI9KG

title: is_networked undefined for Apple

    if (!is_networked(ip4, sizeof(ip4)))

Noticed that is_networked() is defined for ifdef __MINGW32__ or ifndef __APPLE__.

title: rig.h : import  of  <sys/socket.h> breaks the $grig$ build
body:
In version Hamlib-4.6 `rig.h` imports `<sys/socket.h>` . This brings `connect` from `socket.h` into scope.
*grig* imports `rig.h` and at the same time implements some other unrelated `connect` function and
this breaks the build of *grig* with Hamlib-4.6.
Comment in `rig.h` suggest that `<sys/socket.h>` is only needed for internal $Hamlib$ use.

title: Hamlib handles FLRig modes incorrectly

labels.name: Needs test
labels.description: Patches have been submitted but need testing to close issue

body:
Hamlib handles information received from FLRig in an incorrect way.

When I connect QRP Labs QMX transceiver to js8Call (which uses Hamlib to control CAT, even to when accessing through FLRig), I can see two types of errors reported from Hamlib to stderr:

```
Hamlib: flrig_openL Unknown mode (new?) for this rig='DIGI-L'
Hamlib: flrig_openL Unknown mode (new?) for this rig='DIGI-U'
```

The connected rig, QMX, has four possible modes (as of fw 1.0.27): CW, CW-R, DIGI-U and DIGI-L. These are mapped to MD3, MD7, MD6 and MD9 in Kenwood-like command set. The reason why QMX reports DIGI-U and DIGI-L instead of the conventional FSK ans FSK-R is probably due to the fact that QMX is a SDR rig, mostly used for FT8, JS8 and similar modes (single-frequency two-tone FSK or multi-tone MFSK) and has nothing to do with the archaic method of direct keying two-tone FSK. 

So my first objection to Hamlib behavior is that it should accept mode name as-is as it is received from FLRig. It is not up to Hamlib to invent or enforce this. This is correct and true information provided by FLRig.

Later on, Hamlib reports every couple of seconds the following:
```
Hamlib: modeMapGetFLRig: FlRig does not have mode: USB
```
Of course, this is true because QMX indeed has no USB mode (nor it has LSB for that matter), it has DIGI-U instead. This is another thing that Hamlib inapproprietly meddles in - it reports to JS8Call that USB mode is available on the transceiver for JS8 communication, but this is not true, and so when JS8Call requires - via Hamlib to FLRig - that the rig switches to USB mode, it obiously must fail.

I would like to propose the following:

- when talking to FLRig, Hamlib should accept whatever modes are reported by FLRig. The main reason is that Hamlib omits a number of transceiver models while FLRig is pretty up to date, even considering many nuances (e.g. QRP Labs transceivers use enhanced Kenwood command set,  but, for instance, QDX differs from QMX, and FLRig handles them both with astonishing accuracy).
- in general, mode setting (at least), if performed through Hamlib, should be absolutely transparent between the ham software and FLrig because in the current state the Hamlib creates phantom errors that would otherwise not occur.

title: In Python, when using ROT_MODEL_NETROTCTL, rotator ranges are getting zeroed out (or reset), after call to \dump_state
body:
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/39744da7-7610-46dc-93e3-5c97859e6309)

I'm using a Python client to control a Yaesu G-5500 Rotator via a remote rotctld daemon, which is connected to the rotator via a GS-232B USB control interface. If I attempt to set the position of the rotator using the Python client, I get a `range problem` message from set_position():

```
>>> rot.set_position(180.0, 90.0)
rot_set_position called az=180.00 el=90.00
rot_set_position: south_zero=0
rot_set_position: range problem az=180.00(min=0.00,max=0.00), el=90.000000(min=0.00,max=0.000000)
```

The Python client's rotator model, [ROT_MODEL_NETROTCTL](https://github.com/Hamlib/Hamlib/blob/4281a5ef7d32fe9adfb48de6fe52ace7b63e7d6d/rigs/dummy/netrotctl.c#L343), has a default max_el of 90.0, and the remote rotctld rotator ROT_MODEL_GS232B has a max_el of 180.0. Why does Python think my max_el is set to 0.0?

When using ROT_MODEL_NETROTCTL, the max_el, et al, are set in [netrotctl.c](https://github.com/Hamlib/Hamlib/blob/4281a5ef7d32fe9adfb48de6fe52ace7b63e7d6d/rigs/dummy/netrotctl.c#L117)

As best I can tell, the max_el is getting reset, or set to 0.0, when the Python client open()'s a connection and calls /dump_state.

## Steps to Reproduce

On ROTCTLPI:
1. Ensure GS-232B & rotator are connected & powered on.
1. Start rotctld with: `rotctld -m 603 -r /dev/ttyUSB0 -vvvvvv -Z -o -39`

On SIGPI:
1. Ensure Python 3.9 and the Hamlib (python3-hamlib in Debian) library are installed.
2. Run the following Python script:

```python
import Hamlib

rot = Hamlib.Rot(Hamlib.ROT_MODEL_NETROTCTL)
rot.state.rotport.pathname = "ROTCTLPI"
rot.open()
print(rot.state.max_el)
```

## Expected Output

`90.0`

## Actual Output

`0.0`

## Additional Details

### Negative Tests

1. Works: On ROTCTLPI, connecting directly to the GS-232B locally using rotctl.
2. Works: On ROTCTLPI or SIGPI, connecting to rotctld via a remote rotctl client.

title: rigctld reports improper exit code if TCP port is unavailable and does not report error message
body:
### Situation: 

When testing some software I could not start rigctld. Instead of running it exited after a few milliseconds and exit code was 1, no error message was printed on console.

According to documentation exit code 1 means incorrect command line parameter. However, this was not the case. However, the command line was the same as in previous cases when it worked. There was no change in the system or in rigctld version.

Problem was caused by "forgotten" instance of rigctld, i.e. one instance was already running and therefore port 4532 could not be bound and the second instance of rigctld exited with exit code 1.

### Problem(s): 

1. There is no error message in case of this kind of critical error except when verbose command line parameter is selected. 
2. The exit code is 1 but this exit code has a different meaning on documentation. 

### Proposed solution:

1. This kind of condition should be printed to console or log regardless of the selected level of verbosity because it prevents the program to exit immediately and hence it does not provide the expected functionality at all. The user should be informed what os the cause of the critical error.
2. The exit code should not be 1 but a different number and it should be properly noted in the documentation.

### Program version and OS:

title: Feature request: allow TRX selection via TCP command

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

body:
I would like to ask to add TRX selection and init over TCP. The idea is to start rigctld as daemon and control all details from the host application.

1. select serial port. Action: check if the port exists. Response - serial port exists or not.
2. select DTR, RTS state. Action: remember the setup for the subsequent connect. Response - confirm action
3. select serial port baudrate. Action: remember the baudrate for the subsequent connect. Response - confirm action. 
4. select transceiver model. Action: remember for initialization. Response: confirm action.
5. connect and initialize transceiver. Action: connect to serial port and do initialization as is currently done in rigctld. Response: report success or failure, with a reason.

All of the above could also possibly be realized by sending all usual command line arguments as a single string over TCP.

body:
I recently upgraded my Linux test environment to Fedora 42 and it looks like they changed some compiler stuff as well as upgraded Hamlib to 4.6.2. However, that seems to have caused the following build failure in FreeDV:

```
/home/mooneer/freedv-gui/src/rig_control/HamlibRigController.cpp: In static member function ‘static void HamlibRigController::InitializeHamlibLibrary()’:
/home/mooneer/freedv-gui/src/rig_control/HamlibRigController.cpp:180:26: error: invalid conversion from ‘int (*)(rig_caps*, void*)’ to ‘int (*)(const rig_caps*, void*)’ [-fpermissive]
  180 |         rig_list_foreach(&HamlibRigController::BuildRigList_, &RigList_);
      |                          ^~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
      |                          |
      |                          int (*)(rig_caps*, void*)
In file included from /home/mooneer/freedv-gui/src/rig_control/HamlibRigController.h:36,
                 from /home/mooneer/freedv-gui/src/rig_control/HamlibRigController.cpp:32:
/usr/include/hamlib/rig.h:3794:18: note: initializing argument 1 of ‘int rig_list_foreach(int (*)(const rig_caps*, void*), void*)’
 3794 | rig_list_foreach HAMLIB_PARAMS((int (*cfunc)(const struct rig_caps *, rig_ptr_t),
      |                  ^~~~~~~~~~~~~
```

Investigating further, it appears that `RIGCAPS_NOT_CONST` wasn't removed when `const` was readded to `rig_list_foreach` in 4.6.1. It'd be a good idea to do so for 4.6.3, but in the meantime I updated FreeDV to no longer look for that #define and always use the const version (see https://github.com/drowe67/freedv-gui/pull/861/commits/83e080f44aa5d682b619e928e21f5d33efc3990e).

title: License everything under one GPLv3 license (or even better AGPLv3)
body:
The current situation is a mixture of LGPLv2.1+ and GPLv2+ .
https://github.com/Hamlib/Hamlib/blob/master/LICENSE

Copyleft is something great and create basic freedom in the world. Would be great if the whole project could have one GPLv3 license. Or at least have everything under GPLv2 with no LGPL.

It looks like you are currently searching for a GUI: https://github.com/Hamlib/Hamlib/issues/1370
So maybe the front end library that is currently LGPL would also change and make it easy to use one single GPLv3 or at least GPLv2 license for everything.

Because many software projects also at HAM are moving towards web based SAAS, maybe take a look into choosing AGPLv3 for everything.

title: Icom PCR-100 Shutdown command missing or not working. (Solved)
body:
Hi,
I'm making a software with Python to control my Icom PCR-100 Radio. Actually, the program works very well and I use it to switch the radio on and let Gpredict control the frequency for Doppler correction.

To connect my rig I use : 
**subprocess.run("rigctld -v -m 4002 -r /dev/ttyUSB.ICOM-PCR100 -s 38400 -t 4532 -C stop_bits=1 &", shell=True, text=True)**

To change Volume I use : 
 **host = 'localhost'
port = 4532                   # The same port as used by the server
s = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
s.connect((host, port))
s.send(b'L AF 0.3')
s.close()**

But, I didn't succeed to find what I have to do to switch off the radio. 
killing the Rigctld process does not work since my radio is still in receive mode after the commands below :
**rigctld_id=get_pid("rigctld")
os.kill(rigctld_id,9)**
And when I want to connect the radio again it is refused since it is already on.

The documentation said : 
 **0x87, set_powerstat 'Power Status'
              Set power On/Off/Standby 'Power Status'.
              0 = Power Off, 1 = Power On, 2 = Power Standby.  Defined as a bitmask in rig.h.**

So I've tried this code below but it did not work : 

**host = 'localhost'
port = 4532   
s = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
s.connect((host, port))
s.send(b'\x87\x00') 
s.close()**

Can someone help me because I'm wondering whether the shutdown command actually works or whether it has simply not been added to the library for this radio. Perhaps there is something wrong in my code ? Any help is welcome. Thanks in advance.

David.

title: kenwood_send_morse adds an unwanted space at the end of most transmissions
body:
First reported by OK1RR on TLF mailing list for his Elecraft K4. Confirmed by myself on Kenwood TS-590.

The following commands in rigctl can show the problem:

```
b test<cr>
b text<cr>
```

is always sent as 

```
'test text'
```

Problem seems to be the left aligned positioning of the text in the 24 characters space followed by trailing spaces.

Doing some experiments showed that any number of trailing spaces gets compressed to exactly one (additional) space. As soon as the last character in morsebuffer is no space character there will be no additional space sent. Any number of spaces before the text gets ignored.

title: kenwood_transaction() is erroneously stripping eol characters, breaking hamlib for tm-d710/tm-v71a devices.
body:
I was seeing the symptoms reported in #1698. I spent some time debugging the code, and the problem is that by the time we reach this block of code:

https://github.com/Hamlib/Hamlib/blob/aca0b2d1c63eb27b23ce376eaf630da169c17a0a/rigs/kenwood/kenwood.c#L483-L495

We have already called `remove_nonprint(buffer)` at line 448:

https://github.com/Hamlib/Hamlib/blob/aca0b2d1c63eb27b23ce376eaf630da169c17a0a/rigs/kenwood/kenwood.c#L446-L448

This strips the command termination character (`\r`), causing the "Check that command termination is correct" to always fail, effectively breaking hamlib for all TM-D710/TM-V71 type devices.

---

We can confirm this behavior by inspecting the value of `buffer` before and after the call to `remove_nonprint`:

```
Breakpoint 3, kenwood_transaction (rig=rig@entry=0x435d60, cmdstr=cmdstr@entry=0x7ffff740176e "ID", data=data@entry=0x7fffffffc300 "",
    datasize=datasize@entry=128) at kenwood.c:443
443         rig_debug(RIG_DEBUG_TRACE, "%s: read_string len=%d '%s'\n", __func__,
(gdb) p buffer
$1 = "ID TM-V71\r", '\000' <repeats 117 times>
```

This is the `rig_debug` call just before the call to `remove_nonprint`; we can see that the buffer has the `\r` command termination character. After calling `remove_nonprint`...

```
(gdb) until 450
kenwood_transaction (rig=rig@entry=0x435d60, cmdstr=cmdstr@entry=0x7ffff740176e "ID", data=data@entry=0x7fffffffc300 "", datasize=datasize@entry=128)
    at kenwood.c:450
450         if (retval < 0)
(gdb) p buffer
$2 = "ID TM-V71", '\000' <repeats 118 times>
```

...we see that the termination character has been dropped.
