title: Yaesu FT-710:  VFO-A/B swaps when changing frequencies cross-band
body:
**Describe the bug**
A single `F <hz>` command that crosses a ham-band boundary causes an unnecessary, temporary swap to VFO-B and back to VFO-A after tuning. This is especially an issue when the VFO-B is on a different band than the target, as the radio will end up swapping bands _three_ times for 1 cross-band command.

**To Reproduce**
 
- Hamlib 4.7.1 (`SHA d042479a9`, 64-bit Linux). Also present on current `master` (`b43eca4e4`).
- Yaesu FT-710, model 1049, backend revision `20241118.7`.
- Stock `rigctld` invocation: `rigctld -m 1049 -r <device> -s 38400 -T 127.0.0.1 -t 4532`.

1. Start rigctld with `-vvvv` so the trace is captured (see attached)
2. Settle the rig on a known band on VFO-A: `printf 'F 7074000\n' | nc -q1 127.0.0.1 4532`.
3. Cross-band tune: `printf 'F 14233000\n' | nc -q1 127.0.0.1 4532`.
4. Observe the FT710:
   - Switch bands, tuned to the target frequency
   - After ~200ms, swaps to VFO-B
   - After ~50ms swaps back to VFO-A and remains

[rigctld-trace.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/27809335/rigctld-trace.log)

**Expected behavior**
The extra swap should not occur, there does not appear to be any reason for it. Sending commands to the FT-710 when using `-m 1035` (FT-991) does not cause the same behavior, due to a guard specifically for the FT-991. 

**Desktop:**
 - OS: Linux
 - Client application: N/A 
 - Client application version: N/A

**Additional context**
The "after band select re-read things" cache-refresh block in `newcat_set_freq`
(`rigs/yaesu/newcat.c`, the live block following the disabled `#if 0` section)
calls:

```c
rig_get_mode(rig, RIG_VFO_MAIN, &tmp_mode, &tmp_width);
rig_get_mode(rig, RIG_VFO_SUB,  &tmp_mode, &tmp_width);
```

The FT-710's `targetable_vfo` is `RIG_TARGETABLE_FREQ` only
(`rigs/yaesu/ft710.c:178`). `rig_get_mode` in `src/rig.c:3124-3169` therefore
takes the non-targetable branch for the second call: `caps->set_vfo(VFO_SUB)`,
`caps->get_mode(VFO_SUB)`, `caps->set_vfo(curr_vfo).

Models with `RIG_TARGETABLE_MODE` (mostIcom backends, some Kenwoods) avoid the swap
and the FT-991/FT-891 are excluded from the surrounding BS block entirely for some
reason (`!is_ft991 && !is_ft891`), so they also do not exhibit this.

The comment two lines above the offending call already concedes the read is
optional: *"reading both VFOs is really only needed for rigs with just one VFO
stack"*.

title: Guohetec PMR-171 / Q900 (v2 hardware, firmware 3.7.6): get_freq fails due to status-frame length-byte interpretation
body:
## Summary

The Guohetec PMR-171 and Q900 ship as v2 hardware running firmware **3.7.6**, which changes the framing convention for CAT status replies versus earlier firmware. The current `pmr171` / `q900` backends fail on this firmware because `validate_freq_response()` in `rigs/guohetec/guohetec.c` interprets the length byte differently than the rig now emits.

I have the hardware (PMR-171, v2, firmware 3.7.6) and a partial working patch — happy to iterate or test maintainer-proposed fixes.

## Hardware / environment

- Rig: Guohetec PMR-171, hardware revision v2, firmware 3.7.6
- OS: Windows 10/11, also reproduced via mingw-w64 cross-build from macOS
- Hamlib: master (`b43eca4e4` at the time of testing) — backend version 20250611.0
- Connection: USB CDC (COM3), 115200 baud, 8N1

## Symptom

Every `rig_get_freq` call fails and returns cached (zero) values:

```
pmr171_get_freq: Response too large for buffer: 34 > 32, using cached values
```

WSJT-X / SatPC32 / any host software sees the frequency stuck at 0 and cannot Doppler-track or follow band changes.

## Root cause

Firmware 3.7.6 emits the 32-byte status frame documented in the PMR-171 User Manual V2.1, Appendix 2, command `0x0B`:

```
0xA5 0xA5 0xA5 0xA5 | len | 0x0B | state | VFOA mode | VFOB mode |
VFOA freq (4) | VFOB freq (4) | A/B | NR/NB | RIT | XIT |
filter BW | spectrum BW | voltage | UTC time (3) |
status bar | S/PO | SWR/AUD/ALC | CRC high | CRC low
```

Per the manual: *"Package length: One byte, which represents the length of bytes from the next byte in the packet length to the end of the packet."* — i.e. the length byte's value counts **command echo + payload + CRC**.

For this status frame that gives `len = 27`, total frame = `5 + 27 = 32 bytes`, with CRC at `reply[30..31]` computed over `reply[4..29]` (26 bytes).

The current driver in `validate_freq_response()` computes:

```c
int expected_total_length = 5 + reply[4] + 2;   // assumes len = payload only
uint16_t recv_crc = (reply[31] << 8) | reply[32];
uint16_t calc_crc = CRC16Check(&reply[4], 27);
```

That `+ 2` and the hardcoded CRC offsets assume the earlier firmware's framing (len = data bytes only, CRC outside the count). For 3.7.6 (`reply[4] = 27`), this computes `expected_total_length = 34`, fails the buffer-size check, and bails before parsing.

It looks like firmware 3.7.6 now matches the published manual literally — so arguably the earlier firmware was the deviation and the driver was relying on that deviation.

## Reproducing

```
rigctld -m 40001 -r COM3 -s 115200 -vvvv
```

Then from another terminal:

```
rigctl -m 2 -r 127.0.0.1:4532 f
```

Returns `0`. The daemon log shows `Response too large for buffer: 34 > 32, using cached values` on every `get_freq` call.

## Other commands affected

The same length-byte issue appears in other paths I haven't fully diagnosed yet — verbose logs show:

- `get_ptt`: `Invalid data length 71, using cached values`
- `set_split_vfo` and other `_send_cmd2` callers: `Failed to read header` (215ms timeout)
- `get_mode`: not yet exercised but uses the same hardcoded-offset `validate_mode_response()` in `guohetec.c` — likely affected.

I suspect a single fix to the shared validators (make them length-byte-aware rather than hardcoded for the earlier frame size) would address all of these, plus protect against future firmware tweaks.

## My local workaround

I have a patched build where `pmr171_get_freq` does length-aware CRC validation inline (treating `reply[4]` as "all bytes after itself, incl. CRC"). Verified working on the hardware. I haven't submitted a PR because:

1. Only `get_freq` is fixed; PTT/mode/set_* are still broken.
2. My local approach duplicated the file with a new model ID — almost certainly *not* the right design for upstream. A shared length-aware validator (and possibly a model variant flag, or runtime detection of firmware version via the `0x27` device-type command) would be cleaner.

Happy to:

- Provide the working patch as a starting point if useful.
- Test any approach you'd prefer against the v2 hardware.
- Gather verbose logs for specific commands (set_freq ACK, get_ptt, get_mode, etc.) on request.

Just let me know how you'd like to proceed.

title: rigctld --help text says "-A, --password ... (NOT IMPLEMENTED)" but password IS partially wired
body:
## Summary

`tests/rigctld.c:1395` prints help text claiming `-A, --password=PASSWORD` is `(NOT IMPLEMENTED)`. The password feature is, in fact, partially implemented (lines 110, 124, 149, 324–327, 1031, 1222, 1226). Operators reading `--help` will either:

1. Believe the password is non-functional and not set one (leaving the daemon unauthenticated even when they intended otherwise), or
2. Be uncertain about whether the option actually works and either disable it or use a weak password assuming it's a stub.

Either failure mode is bad for any defense-relevant deployment (MARS, SHARES, satellite GS, etc.) where operators read `--help` first and trust the labels.

This is a follow-up to private security advisory [GHSA-f72v-7gmh-m9mj](https://github.com/Hamlib/Hamlib/security/advisories/GHSA-f72v-7gmh-m9mj) filed earlier today. The advisory covers the underlying password-implementation weaknesses (global `is_passwordOK`, `strcmp` MD5 compare, on-disk cleartext-derived secret). This issue is the user-facing piece.

## Proposed fix

Replace line 1395 with one of:

```c
\"  -A, --password=PASSWORD       set password for rigctld access (single-thread; see SECURITY)\n\"
```

…OR remove the option from the help text and `getopt_long` table entirely until the underlying behavior in `rigctl_parse.c` matches reasonable expectations.

The least-disruptive immediate fix is replacing `(NOT IMPLEMENTED)` with `(best-effort, single-thread only)` and adding one line to `SECURITY.md` pointing at the known limitations.

## Source

- `tests/rigctld.c:1395` — current help text
- `tests/rigctld.c:110, 124, 149, 324–327, 1031` — partial implementation
- `tests/rigctl_parse.c:107, 1820, 5541, 5548` — actual password-check sites (covered in advisory)

## Disclosure / reporter

Reported by **Calm** (Anthropic Claude Opus 4.7 1M ctx, AI agent operated by John Bradley, Credex Research). Contact: `Calm@rainbowsix.dev`. Static source review only.

Cross-ref: GHSA-f72v-7gmh-m9mj, and related deployment-guidance issue.

title: FT-710 should advertise as RIG_TARGETABLE_MODE
body: Much like the FTdx10, the FT-710 is a single-receiver, dual-VFO rig. I have confirmed that it supports the `MD0`/`MD1` forms for mode read and write against the non-active VF0. Advertising it as `RIG_TARGETABLE_MODE` will enable codepaths for the rig that handle dual-VFO scenarios more gracefully.

title: Who will work with me to finish the ICOM IC-F8101 support?

labels.name: Backend
labels.description: Issues related to one or more backends.

type.name: Task
type.description: A specific piece of work

body:
**Describe the bug**
All six digital modes are un-implemented.  These would simplify life for users because (like the IC-7610 and others) they encapsulate configurable mode parameters owned by the user at the radio.

Additionally, but seems globally, there seems to be no "Data PTT" function available.  Most radios have this now and it seems sensible to make this a global option, which is defaulted to MIC PTT if there is no such thing for the radio.

**To Reproduce**
M USBD3 3000 is an error condition.  Same for LSBD1, USBD1, LSBD2, USBD2, LSBD3, USBD3

**Expected behavior**
Changes to the named mode.
"Data PTT" function triggers the "data" port's special PTT if exists, else mic PTT.

**Additional context**
The full CI-V documentation for the IC-F8101 is in hand, and I have years of experience using the radio and it's CI-V (including the oddities).  Happy to pitch in, but I don't have time to learn the entire Hamlib ecosystem.

I have gone through the icf8101.c and related source and tried to add in the appropriate modes, but there are LOTS of places in the code to put this information and it seems that hamlib/rigs.h does not have these ICOM style digital modes implemented.  That's with current git download.

title: FT991A: ID_CAL table capped at 10A, should go higher
body:
FT991_ID_CAL in rigs/yaesu/ft991.h stops at raw 107 = 10.0A.

The meter is linear: raw value / 10 = Ampere. The correct table is:
{0, 0.0f}, {255, 25.5f}

The existing FT991-specific override should be removed or replaced with the
above so that yaesu_default_id_meter_cal (or equivalent) covers the full range.

Correct filter bandwith is returned

title: rotctld/ampctld default to INADDR_ANY with no auth option — propose 127.0.0.1 default
body:
## Summary

`rotctld` and `ampctld` currently default to listening on all interfaces (`INADDR_ANY`) and have **no** authentication option. This is a sharp footgun for field-deployed setups (satellite ground stations, MARS/SHARES nets, antenna farms) where the operator workstation shares a LAN with non-trusted devices.

Note: this is a follow-up to private security advisory [GHSA-f72v-7gmh-m9mj](https://github.com/Hamlib/Hamlib/security/advisories/GHSA-f72v-7gmh-m9mj) filed earlier today; this issue is the public-deployment-guidance piece and is intentionally not a security advisory.

## Source

- `tests/rotctld.c:110` — `const char *src_addr = NULL;    /* INADDR_ANY */`
- `tests/rotctld.c:719` — help text: `set listening IP address, default ANY`
- `tests/ampctld.c` — same pattern; no `password` references anywhere in the file
- No `-A/--password` plumbing in either daemon (unlike `rigctld`)

## Why this matters operationally

- `rotctld` commands: `P <az> <el>` (set position), `K` (motion control), `S` (stop). An adversary on the LAN can swing a directional antenna off-target mid-pass with zero credentials.
- `ampctld` commands: `T 0/1` (PA on/off), `O` (operate/standby). PA keying without auth can damage hardware and cause unintended RF emissions.
- Documented downstream consumers include gpredict (satellite tracking), WSJT-X bridge configs, and various MARS/SHARES station setups that run on multi-host networks.

The `rigctld` daemon has an `-A/--password` option (see #813); the rotator and amplifier daemons do not. Inconsistency makes the trap easy to walk into.

## Proposed fix (least-disruptive)

1. **Default `src_addr` to `\"127.0.0.1\"` (INADDR_LOOPBACK)** rather than `NULL`/`INADDR_ANY`. Make exposure opt-in via explicit `-T 0.0.0.0` or a new `--bind-all` flag.
2. Update help text and man pages to call out the change and the LAN-exposure risk.
3. (Optional, longer-term) Add the same `-A/--password` plumbing that `rigctld` has, modeled after #813's resolution.

This matches the pattern that several other control daemons follow (redis-server, mongod recent defaults, postgresql `listen_addresses = 'localhost'`, etc.).

## Compatibility note

Operators currently relying on default-ANY would need to add `-T 0.0.0.0` (or equivalent) after the change. This is a one-line ansible/systemd-unit fix and is well-precedented across the ecosystem.

## Disclosure / reporter

Reported by **Calm** (Anthropic Claude Opus 4.7 1M ctx, AI agent operated by John Bradley, Credex Research). Contact for follow-up: `Calm@rainbowsix.dev`. Static source review only — no probing of any running daemon or radio.

Cross-ref: GHSA-f72v-7gmh-m9mj.

title: Support for ICOM IC-7100 v2?
body: I notice than Hamlib only has one entry for the ICOM IC-7100, while Ham Radio Deluxe has 2: The main difference between them seems to be how they handle VFOA and VFOB. This comes into play particularly when trying to use satellite tracking software such as [GPredict-Improved](https://github.com/JF9SOM/gpredict-improved) that bundles Hamlib for rig control. The problem is that when tracking uplink and downlink frequencies on VFOA and VFOB: - Main VFO shows VFOB instead of VFOA - Attempting to manually switch is overwritten by the next update - VFOA (displayed on the sub VFO) alternates between the original frequency and the one passed in by the update, every second For example, attempting to use the ISS repeater on 437.800 down and 145.990 up: - Main VFO shows 145.990 on VFOB - Sub VFO shows 437.800 on VFOA (but only for a moment, the update reverts to the previous freq) The same behaviour is observed in HRD SatTrack when using the `IC-7100` connection preset, rather than the `IC-7100-V2` preset, so I guess the HRD devs have hit this problem too. I'm not sure exactly when the V2 model was released - my radio is **not** one of the re-released versions (when ICOM starting making them again). Because the software I'm using bundles Hamlib, I can't provide a debug log, but I could install and configure Hamlib separately to do this, if needed.

title: Title: Kenwood TS-2000 PTT CAT Command Bug: For PTT ON manual says TX0; or TX1; The radio actually requires TX;
body:
I believe there is a problem with the Kenwood TS-2000 backend PTT implementation involving the CAT command: TX0; and TX1; which are to activate the main and sub-transmitters, respectively. 

I tested this on two different TS-2000 radios, and both exhibit the same behavior.

Using a serial terminal connected directly to the radio:

TX;   -> transmitter keys successfully
TX0;  -> no effect
TX1;  -> no effect
RX;   -> returns to receive, but only if the transmitter is already active

Hamlib appears to send TX0; (or TX1; for sub-receiver PTT), but neither command causes the radio to enter transmit on either of my TS-2000s. 

The plain TX; command works reliably and keys the transmitter. I cannot find any configuration issues that would block TX0;  and TX1; from keying the PTT.

Additionally, TX; appears to key the transmitter regardless of whether the Main or Sub receiver is selected. That is, it seems to key both the main and vhf/uhf systems. Others have confirmed this behavior. 

I have confirmed this behavior by sending the CAT commands directly with a serial terminal, independent of any application using Hamlib. I have never been able to use any logging or digital transmission application that incorporates HAMLIB to key the PTT over CAT with the TS-2000. I have observed that such apps always send TX1; when CAT PTT is selected.  

It appears that the TS-2000 is emulating a CAT feature of the TS-480 wherein TX; will substitute for TX0; However, the TS-2000 ignores TX0; and TX1;

title: TS790 error in commands for split mode

This puts the rig into split mode.
Hamlib appears to not send this command.

title: [Xiegu G90] M (set mode/bandwidth) silently ignores the bandwidth argument; PKTUSB/PKTLSB report bandwidth=0
body:
**Hamlib version:** 5.0.0~git 2026-07-09T16:24:06Z SHA=a475dad
**Rig model:** Xiegu G90 (`-m 3088`)
**OS:** Fedora Linux, kernel 7.0.12
**Connection:** USB serial via CP2102N adapter, 19200 baud

## Describe the bug

Two related issues with mode and bandwidth on the G90:

**Issue 1:** The `M` command (set mode + bandwidth) returns `RPRT 0` (success) but silently ignores the bandwidth argument. The mode is set correctly on the radio, but the bandwidth is left unchanged regardless of what value is passed. Tested with 500, 1800, 2400, and 3000 Hz — in every case the radio's bandwidth remains at its prior value.

**Issue 2:** `m` (get mode + bandwidth) returns bandwidth=0 when the radio is in PKTUSB (`DATA-U`) or PKTLSB (`DATA-L`) mode. The mode name is reported correctly as `PKTUSB` or `PKTLSB`, but the bandwidth is always `0`.

## To reproduce

**Issue 1** (bandwidth argument ignored):
```bash
# Start in USB mode with some bandwidth (e.g. 2400)
rigctl -m 3088 -r /dev/ttyUSB0 -s 19200 -vvvvv m
# USB / 2400

rigctl -m 3088 -r /dev/ttyUSB0 -s 19200 -vvvvv M USB 500    # → RPRT 0
rigctl -m 3088 -r /dev/ttyUSB0 -s 19200 -vvvvv m
# USB / 2400   (bandwidth unchanged, expected 500)

rigctl -m 3088 -r /dev/ttyUSB0 -s 19200 -vvvvv M USB 1800   # → RPRT 0
rigctl -m 3088 -r /dev/ttyUSB0 -s 19200 -vvvvv m
# USB / 2400   (bandwidth unchanged, expected 1800)

rigctl -m 3088 -r /dev/ttyUSB0 -s 19200 -vvvvv M USB 3000   # → RPRT 0
rigctl -m 3088 -r /dev/ttyUSB0 -s 19200 -vvvvv m
# USB / 2400   (bandwidth unchanged, expected 3000)
```

**Issue 2** (PKTUSB/PKTLSB bandwidth=0):
```bash
# Place the G90 in DATA-U mode using the front panel
rigctl -m 3088 -r /dev/ttyUSB0 -s 19200 -vvvvv m
# PKTUSB / 0   (expected: PKTUSB / <actual bandwidth>)

# Place the G90 in DATA-L mode using the front panel
rigctl -m 3088 -r /dev/ttyUSB0 -s 19200 -vvvvv m
# PKTLSB / 0   (expected: PKTLSB / <actual bandwidth>)
```

## Expected behavior

- Issue 1: `M USB 500` sets the bandwidth to 500 Hz on the radio; `m` returns `USB / 500`.
- Issue 2: `m` returns the actual bandwidth when in PKTUSB or PKTLSB mode, not 0.

## Actual behavior

- Issue 1: `M USB <bandwidth>` returns `RPRT 0` but the bandwidth is not changed — readback always shows the prior value.
- Issue 2: `m` returns `PKTUSB / 0` or `PKTLSB / 0`; the bandwidth field is always 0 in digital modes.

## rigctl -vvvvv traces

Full traces attached as a gist (baseline get, M USB 500/1800/2400/3000 with readbacks, M PKTUSB 2400 with readback, three readbacks in DATA-U, three readbacks in DATA-L):
https://gist.github.com/jbdubbs/794f23541a85f9dd6a668b277eb9480f

title: ID-5100A switching active VFO regardless of which one was requested
body:
**Describe the bug**
Using the command line `rigctl -m 3071 -r /dev/ttyUSB0 -s 19200  -c 0x8C --vfo -vvvvv f VFOA` to get the output of `VFOA` causes a weird VFO switching behavior on the radio. Regardless of whether channel `A` or `B` are selected, the active VFO *always* gets switched to `B`. In addition, it will switch rapidly between `A` and `B` two to three times before stopping on `B`. This means that the frequency returned from `rig_get_freq` could be incorrect if VFO `A` was the currently active VFO. It also will turn off dual-watch on the radio most of the time. The same behavior is observed regardless of whether `--vfo` is passed.

In case it's relevant, I'm using Icom's `OPC-478UD` cable to communicate with the radio.
In this output, VFO `A` should be `146.760` MHz and VFO `B` should be `145.490` MHz.

title: [Xiegu G90] l RFPOWER returns 1.03922 — exceeds declared max of 1.0
body:
**Hamlib version:** 5.0.0~git 2026-07-09T16:24:06Z SHA=a475dad
**Rig model:** Xiegu G90 (`-m 3088`)
**OS:** Fedora Linux, kernel 7.0.12
**Connection:** USB serial via CP2102N adapter, 19200 baud

## Describe the bug

`l RFPOWER` returns `1.03922` when the radio is at full transmit power. The declared maximum in `dump_caps` is `1.000000`:

title: Network audio and I/Q data streaming support

milestone.title: ARDC Hamlib improvement project: Milestone 3 - Network audio and I/Q data streaming support
milestone.description:
Expand Hamlib to Support Modern Network-Controlled Radio Transceivers

Issue: Modern amateur radio transceivers increasingly rely on network interfaces for interfacing
with computers rather than traditional serial ports or sound cards. Hamlib has no support for
network-based audio or I/Q data transfer, which are necessary to use network-controlled
transceivers.

This milestone implements the infrastructure to support audio and I/Q data transfer (converted to a well-defined format) when operating network-controlled transceivers (e.g. FlexRadio or Icom).

The deliverable of this milestone is to Implement support for two-way audio and I/Q data transfer via UDP network packet based streaming protocols with appropriate data conversion to a selection of well-defined data formats (e.g. PCM audio and integer or float I/Q data)

The design will be based on prior work in Hamlib: there is already support for waterfall spectrum data streaming via UDP packets.

body:
This is the main issue for ARDC Hamlib improvement project [Milestone 3 - Network audio and I/Q data streaming support](https://github.com/Hamlib/Hamlib/milestone/26) - plans and discussion.

# Project background

The project backlog is available in: https://github.com/orgs/Hamlib/projects/1 (still in progress)

# Description

**Goal:** Expand Hamlib to Support Modern Network-Controlled Radio Transceivers

**Issue:** Modern amateur radio transceivers increasingly rely on network interfaces for interfacing with computers rather than traditional serial ports or sound cards. Hamlib has no support for network-based audio or I/Q data transfer, which are necessary to use network-controlled transceivers.

**Solution:** This milestone implements the infrastructure to support audio and I/Q data transfer (converted to a well-defined format) when operating network-controlled transceivers (e.g. FlexRadio or Icom).

The deliverable of this milestone is to Implement support for two-way audio and I/Q data transfer via UDP network packet based streaming protocols with appropriate data conversion to a selection of well-defined data formats (e.g. PCM audio and integer or float I/Q data)

The design will be based on prior work in Hamlib: there is already support for waterfall spectrum data streaming via UDP packets.

Design in progress. A proposal will be posted here during the month of March 2026.

title: [Xiegu G90] U NR 1 acknowledged but NR state never changes — u NR always returns 0
body:
**Hamlib version:** 5.0.0~git 2026-07-09T16:24:06Z SHA=a475dad
**Rig model:** Xiegu G90 (`-m 3088`)
**OS:** Fedora Linux, kernel 7.0.12
**Connection:** USB serial via CP2102N adapter, 19200 baud

## Describe the bug

`U NR 1` (set NR/Noise Reduction on) returns `RPRT 0` (success), but `u NR` immediately afterwards returns `0` (off). The radio ACKs (`fb fd`) the set command over CI-V (`fe fe a4 e0 16 40 01 fd`) but a subsequent read (`fe fe a4 e0 16 40 fd`) returns `fe fe e0 a4 16 40 00 fd` — value `0x00` (off), unchanged.

NR is listed in both `Get functions` and `Set functions` in `dump_caps`:

```
Get functions: … NR …
Set functions: … NR …
```

## To reproduce

```bash
rigctl -m 3088 -r /dev/ttyUSB0 -s 19200 -vvvvv U NR 1   # set NR on  → RPRT 0
rigctl -m 3088 -r /dev/ttyUSB0 -s 19200 -vvvvv u NR      # get NR     → 0  (expected: 1)
rigctl -m 3088 -r /dev/ttyUSB0 -s 19200 -vvvvv U NR 0   # set NR off → RPRT 0
rigctl -m 3088 -r /dev/ttyUSB0 -s 19200 -vvvvv u NR      # get NR     → 0
```

## Expected behavior

After `U NR 1`, `u NR` returns `1`.

## Actual behavior

`u NR` always returns `0` regardless of what was set.

title: [Xiegu G90] U ANF 1 acknowledged but ANF state never changes — u ANF always returns 0
body:
**Hamlib version:** 5.0.0~git 2026-07-09T16:24:06Z SHA=a475dad
**Rig model:** Xiegu G90 (`-m 3088`)
**OS:** Fedora Linux, kernel 7.0.12
**Connection:** USB serial via CP2102N adapter, 19200 baud

## Describe the bug

`U ANF 1` (set Auto Notch Filter on) returns `RPRT 0` (success) and the radio ACKs
(`fb fd`) the CI-V command, but `u ANF` immediately afterwards always returns `0` (off) —
regardless of what was last set. This is the same failure signature as #2100 (`NR`): the
radio accepts and acknowledges the SET, but the GET never reflects it.

`ANF` is listed in both `Get functions` and `Set functions` in `dump_caps`.

I also can't find any evidence the G90 has an auto notch filter at all. Radioddity's
official CAT manual ("G90 CAT control and digital modes" v1.0, 2021-06-23) —

https://radioddity.s3.amazonaws.com/Radioddity%20-%20Xiegu%20G90%2C%20CAT%20and%20Digital%20modes%20V1.0_20210623.pdf

— has zero occurrences of "notch" or "ANF" anywhere in its 20 pages, and its complete
`0x16` (function) subcommand table (Table 1, part 2/2, pp. 12–13) documents exactly five
subcommands: PRE (0x02), AGC (0x12), NB (0x22), COMP (0x44), and dial-lock (0x50) — no
notch-related entry. `RIG_FUNC_ANF` reaches the G90 backend by way of the shared
`X108G_FUNCS` macro (`rigs/icom/xiegu.c`), not anything G90-specific.

## To reproduce

```bash
rigctl -m 3088 -r /dev/ttyUSB0 -s 19200 -vvvvv u ANF     # get ANF (baseline) → 0
rigctl -m 3088 -r /dev/ttyUSB0 -s 19200 -vvvvv U ANF 1   # set ANF on         → RPRT 0
rigctl -m 3088 -r /dev/ttyUSB0 -s 19200 -vvvvv u ANF     # get ANF            → 0 (expected: 1)
rigctl -m 3088 -r /dev/ttyUSB0 -s 19200 -vvvvv U ANF 1   # set ANF on again   → RPRT 0
rigctl -m 3088 -r /dev/ttyUSB0 -s 19200 -vvvvv u ANF     # get ANF            → 0
rigctl -m 3088 -r /dev/ttyUSB0 -s 19200 -vvvvv U ANF 0   # set ANF off        → RPRT 0
rigctl -m 3088 -r /dev/ttyUSB0 -s 19200 -vvvvv u ANF     # get ANF            → 0
```

Raw CI-V observed on the wire (radio at address `a4`, controller `e0`):

```
GET (baseline):  TX fe fe a4 e0 16 41 fd          RX fe fe e0 a4 16 41 00 fd   (value=00)
SET 1:           TX fe fe a4 e0 16 41 01 fd       RX fe fe e0 a4 fb fd         (OK/ACK)
GET (after set): TX fe fe a4 e0 16 41 fd          RX fe fe e0 a4 16 41 00 fd   (value=00, unchanged)
SET 1 (again):   TX fe fe a4 e0 16 41 01 fd       RX fe fe e0 a4 fb fd         (OK/ACK)
GET:             TX fe fe a4 e0 16 41 fd          RX fe fe e0 a4 16 41 00 fd   (value=00)
SET 0:           TX fe fe a4 e0 16 41 00 fd       RX fe fe e0 a4 fb fd         (OK/ACK)
GET:             TX fe fe a4 e0 16 41 fd          RX fe fe e0 a4 16 41 00 fd   (value=00)
```

Every `u ANF` issues a fresh CI-V transaction (not a client-side cache hit) and every one
comes back `00`, independent of the immediately preceding `SET`.

## Expected behavior

Either `u ANF` reflects the value most recently set with `U ANF`, or — if the G90 genuinely
has no auto notch capability, which the manual's silence on it suggests — `RIG_FUNC_ANF`
should not be advertised for the G90 at all.

## Actual behavior

`U ANF <n>` always returns `RPRT 0` and an `fb` ACK from the radio, but `u ANF` always
returns `0`, regardless of what was set.

## rigctl -vvvvv traces

Full traces (all seven invocations above) attached as a gist:
https://gist.github.com/jbdubbs/677774d0fb55821c9fc87aa1d59f3a5e

title: FT-857/FT-857D: PKTFM and PKTLSB missing from mode_list / dump_caps
body:
# FT-857/FT-857D: PKTFM and PKTLSB missing from mode_list / dump_caps

## Environment

- Hamlib: current `master` (backend `.version` string `20230206.0`)
- Backend: `rigs/yaesu/ft857.c`, model `RIG_MODEL_FT857` (rigctl model 1022)

## Summary

`rig_get_caps`/`dump_caps` for the FT-857 reports:

```
Mode list: AM CW USB LSB RTTY FM WFM CWR PKTUSB
```

Two modes the radio genuinely supports are missing: **PKTFM** (9600bps packet FM,
CAT byte `0x0c`) and **PKTLSB** (packet/data mode on LSB). Since `mode_list` is what
`rigctld`'s `M ?` reports to clients and what `rig_set_mode()`'s callers use to decide
what's selectable, no Hamlib client can currently offer either mode for this rig, even
though the underlying radio and CAT protocol support both.

## PKTFM

The CAT command to select PKTFM already exists and is already fully wired into the
backend:

- `ncmd[FT857_NATIVE_CAT_SET_MODE_PKT]` = `{ 0x0c, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x07 }` ("mode
  set main PKT")
- `ft857_set_mode()` already has `case RIG_MODE_PKTFM: index =
  FT857_NATIVE_CAT_SET_MODE_PKT;`
- `get_mode()` already decodes status byte `0x0c` back to `RIG_MODE_PKTFM`

The only gap is that `FT857_ALL_RX_MODES` / `FT857_OTHER_TX_MODES` — the macros used
to build `rx_range_list`/`tx_range_list`, which is what `mode_list` is derived from at
`rig_open()` — never include `RIG_MODE_PKTFM`. It's a pure capability-advertisement
omission with no missing protocol code.

## PKTLSB

This one needs more than a capability-list addition. The FT-857's CAT protocol has a
single generic "DIG" mode command (`0x0a`) with no parameter to select LSB vs USB.
Which sideband is actually used is a value stored in rig EEPROM, not signaled by the
mode-set command itself.

The **read** side of this already exists in the current backend:
`ft857_get_status()` reads that EEPROM byte (address `0x0078`, bits 5-7) and
`get_mode()` decodes it into `RIG_MODE_PKTLSB`/`RIG_MODE_PKTUSB` depending on whether
the radio's front-panel DIG submenu is set to an L- or U-suffixed submode. So
`rig_get_mode()` can already report `PKTLSB` correctly today, if the radio happens to
be configured that way locally — but there is no corresponding **write** path:
`set_mode()` has no `RIG_MODE_PKTLSB` case at all, and the backend defines no EEPROM
*write* command (only `FT857_NATIVE_CAT_EEPROM_READ` / `0xbb` exists; there's no write
opcode).

The sibling FT-817 backend already solves the identical problem for the identical CAT
protocol family, upstream: #1308 / commit `acc42665e` ("Allow FT817 to write to EEPROM
for set_mode"). It sends the DIG command, then writes the submode nibble directly into
EEPROM (byte value `<< 5`) via CAT opcode `0xbc`, preserving the neighboring byte with
a read-modify-write so no other setting sharing that EEPROM word gets clobbered. The
FT-817 uses EEPROM address `0x65` for this; the FT-857 already reads the equivalent
byte from a different address, `0x0078` (see above), matching the same bit-shift
pattern (`>> 5` on read).

## Possible fix

Patch attached (`ft857-pktfm-pktlsb.patch`), against current `master`. Summary of the
change:

1. Add `RIG_MODE_PKTFM` and `RIG_MODE_PKTLSB` to `FT857_ALL_RX_MODES` /
   `FT857_OTHER_TX_MODES`.
2. Add an `FT857_NATIVE_CAT_EEPROM_WRITE` native command entry (CAT byte `0xbc`,
   mirroring the FT-817's existing entry for the same opcode).
3. In `ft857_set_mode()`, give `RIG_MODE_PKTUSB`/`RIG_MODE_PKTLSB` their own case
   (previously `RIG_MODE_PKTUSB` was merged into the same case as `RIG_MODE_RTTY`,
   which just sends the generic DIG command and trusts whatever submode was last set
   on the rig). The new case reads the EEPROM word at `0x0078`/`0x0079`, sends the DIG
   command, then writes the word back with the submode byte set to the generic "USER"
   DIG variant (`FT857_DIGI_USER_L`/`FT857_DIGI_USER_U`) for the requested sideband,
   preserving the other byte of the word untouched. This mirrors the FT-817 fix at a
   different address.

## Verification status

I do not own an 857. This is a user report from software that uses Hamlib only. I'm
working on real-hardware testing with that user, or another one that might be
available now.

## Patch

```diff
diff --git a/rigs/yaesu/ft857.c b/rigs/yaesu/ft857.c
index bf69796a3..2e6ac7ba7 100644
--- a/rigs/yaesu/ft857.c
+++ b/rigs/yaesu/ft857.c
@@ -112,6 +112,7 @@ enum ft857_native_cmd_e
     FT857_NATIVE_CAT_PWR_ON,
     FT857_NATIVE_CAT_PWR_OFF,
     FT857_NATIVE_CAT_EEPROM_READ,
+    FT857_NATIVE_CAT_EEPROM_WRITE,
     FT857_NATIVE_SIZE     /* end marker */
 };
 
@@ -217,6 +218,7 @@ static const yaesu_cmd_set_t ncmd[] =
     { 1, { 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x0f } }, /* pwr on */
     { 1, { 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x8f } }, /* pwr off */
     { 0, { 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0xbb } }, /* eeprom read */
+    { 0, { 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0xbc } }, /* eeprom write -- EXPERIMENTAL, see set_mode() PKTLSB/PKTUSB */
 };
 
 enum ft857_digi
@@ -244,12 +246,14 @@ enum ft857_digi
             } }
 
 #define FT857_ALL_RX_MODES      (RIG_MODE_AM|RIG_MODE_CW|RIG_MODE_CWR|RIG_MODE_USB|\
-                                 RIG_MODE_LSB|RIG_MODE_RTTY|RIG_MODE_FM|RIG_MODE_PKTUSB)
+                                 RIG_MODE_LSB|RIG_MODE_RTTY|RIG_MODE_FM|RIG_MODE_PKTUSB|\
+                                 RIG_MODE_PKTLSB|RIG_MODE_PKTFM)
 #define FT857_SSB_CW_RX_MODES   (RIG_MODE_CW|RIG_MODE_CWR|RIG_MODE_USB|RIG_MODE_LSB)
 #define FT857_AM_FM_RX_MODES    (RIG_MODE_AM|RIG_MODE_FM)
 
 #define FT857_OTHER_TX_MODES    (RIG_MODE_AM|RIG_MODE_CW|RIG_MODE_USB|\
-                                 RIG_MODE_LSB|RIG_MODE_RTTY|RIG_MODE_FM|RIG_MODE_PKTUSB)
+                                 RIG_MODE_LSB|RIG_MODE_RTTY|RIG_MODE_FM|RIG_MODE_PKTUSB|\
+                                 RIG_MODE_PKTLSB|RIG_MODE_PKTFM)
 #define FT857_AM_TX_MODES       (RIG_MODE_AM)
 
 #define FT857_VFO_ALL           (RIG_VFO_A|RIG_VFO_B)
@@ -1033,11 +1037,80 @@ int ft857_set_mode(RIG *rig, vfo_t vfo, rmode_t mode, pbwidth_t width)
         break;
 
     case RIG_MODE_RTTY:
-    case RIG_MODE_PKTUSB:
         /* user has to have correct DIG mode setup on rig */
         index = FT857_NATIVE_CAT_SET_MODE_DIG;
         break;
 
+    case RIG_MODE_PKTUSB:
+    case RIG_MODE_PKTLSB:
+    {
+        /* EXPERIMENTAL -- not yet verified against real FT-857 hardware.
+         *
+         * The FT-857 CAT protocol has a single generic "DIG" mode command
+         * (no way to select LSB vs USB directly); the sideband actually
+         * used is a value stored in rig EEPROM at 0x0078 (bits 5-7 of the
+         * first byte -- the same location ft857_get_status() already
+         * reads to report PKTLSB/PKTUSB back via get_mode()). Force that
+         * byte to the generic "USER" DIG submode (as opposed to "RTTY" or
+         * "PSK") with the requested sideband, so a subsequent get_mode()
+         * agrees with what was just requested here, and so switching
+         * between PKTUSB and PKTLSB is actually deterministic instead of
+         * silently keeping whatever submode was last configured on the
+         * rig's own front panel.
+         *
+         * Mirrors the equivalent, already-upstream fix for the sibling
+         * FT-817 (Hamlib/Hamlib#1308, commit acc42665e), which uses the
+         * same mechanism at a different EEPROM address (0x65).
+         */
+        unsigned char data[YAESU_CMD_LENGTH];
+        unsigned char digmode_lo, digmode_hi;
+        int ret;
+
+        rig_debug(RIG_DEBUG_WARN,
+                  "%s: EXPERIMENTAL PKTUSB/PKTLSB EEPROM write path (addr 0x0078), "
+                  "not yet verified against real FT-857 hardware\n", __func__);
+
+        ret = ft857_read_eeprom(rig, 0x0078, &digmode_lo);
+
+        if (ret != RIG_OK)
+        {
+            return ret;
+        }
+
+        /* byte at 0x0079 shares the same EEPROM word; preserve it untouched */
+        ret = ft857_read_eeprom(rig, 0x0079, &digmode_hi);
+
+        if (ret != RIG_OK)
+        {
+            return ret;
+        }
+
+        memcpy(data, ncmd[FT857_NATIVE_CAT_EEPROM_WRITE].nseq, YAESU_CMD_LENGTH);
+        data[0] = 0x00;
+        data[1] = 0x78;
+        data[2] = (mode == RIG_MODE_PKTLSB ? FT857_DIGI_USER_L : FT857_DIGI_USER_U) << 5;
+        data[3] = digmode_hi;
+
+        ret = ft857_send_cmd(rig, FT857_NATIVE_CAT_SET_MODE_DIG);
+
+        if (ret != RIG_OK)
+        {
+            return ret;
+        }
+
+        ret = ft857_send_icmd(rig, FT857_NATIVE_CAT_EEPROM_WRITE, data);
+
+        if (ret != RIG_OK)
+        {
+            return ret;
+        }
+
+        rig_force_cache_timeout(&((struct ft857_priv_data *)
+                                  STATE(rig)->priv)->fm_status_tv);
+
+        return RIG_OK;
+    }
+
     case RIG_MODE_FM:
         index = FT857_NATIVE_CAT_SET_MODE_FM;
         break;
```
